endorsements.issuer: ACR, CAR, ESR, RANZCR, RSNA; Radiol Artif Intell 2024 (PMID 38251899, doi:10.1148/ryai.230513)

endorsements.quote: Minimum evaluation: Observational human-AI interaction studies in simulated or live settings measuring decision change, task time, false positive-driven unnecessary interventions, and clinician trust/usability in accordance to standardized scales.

endorsements.quote: A central point was that the gold standard for evaluating impact is not “AI vs human” but “human vs human plus AI” in real workflows.

endorsements.quote: The group stressed that AI should be evaluated as a co-intervention, acknowledging its potential to influence patient engagement and clinician decisions.

endorsements.quote: This phase typically employs a multidimensional framework based on prospective randomized controlled trials (Method 6), which use controlled comparisons to eliminate confounding and ensure that any observed benefit can be causally attributed to AI 110 , 111 .

endorsements.title: The benchmark illusion: on the curious underestimation of AI and the uncertainty of its creators' gold standards
endorsements.quote: Standardized prospective studies should compare AI-assisted clinicians with those using conventional resources against definitive clinical endpoints, rather than against each other's labels.

evidence.title: Artificial Intelligence-based Automated Echocardiographic Analysis and the Workflow of Sonographers: A randomized crossover trial
evidence.outcome: Sonographer performance with versus without AI in deployment mode, including agreement with final expert-endorsed values
evidence.effect: Randomized AI-assisted vs manual days; AI measurements within acceptable clinical limits of final expert-endorsed values for 90% of parameters; parameters analyzed 85 vs 25.
evidence.quote: Differences between AI-generated measurements and final expert-endorsed values were within acceptable clinical limits for 90% of parameters.

evidence.title: An agentic AI system enhances clinical detection of immunotherapy toxicities: a multi-phase validation study
evidence.outcome: Annotation time, accuracy, agreement for staff with vs without agentic AI assistance
evidence.effect: Randomized crossover (17 participants, 316 observations): time reduced 40% (P<0.001), complete-match accuracy OR 1.45 (95% CI 1.01–2.09; P=0.045), Krippendorff's α from 0.22–0.51 to 0.82–0.85
evidence.quote: In a randomized crossover study of clinical trial staff (17 participants, 316 observations), agentic assistance reduced annotation time by 40% (P < 0.001), increased complete-match accuracy (OR 1.45; 95% CI 1.01–2.09; P = 0.045), and improved inter-annotator agreement (Krippendorff’s α from 0.22–0.51 to 0.82–0.85).
evidence.sample_unit: clinical trial staff participants (316 observations; plus 263 retrospective and 884 prospective notes)

evidence.title: Evidence-grounded AI for longitudinal clinical management in musculoskeletal care
evidence.outcome: Full-chain management success for physicians with AI in prospective decision-making study
evidence.effect: OrthoPilot increased full-chain management success by 10.6% across 1,870 complex cases.
evidence.quote: In a prospective physician decision-making study of 1,870 complex cases, OrthoPilot increased full-chain management success by 10.6%.

evidence.title: AI Improves Nodule Detection on Chest Radiographs in a Health Screening Population: A Randomized Controlled Trial
evidence.outcome: Radiologist performance with versus without AI assistance in the intended deployment mode
evidence.effect: Radiologists referring to AI results detected more actionable nodules (0.59% vs 0.25%) with similar false-referral rates (45.9% vs 56.0%, P = .14) and positive-report rates (2.3% vs 1.9%, P = .14).
evidence.quote: The AI and non-AI groups showed similar false-referral rates (45.9% [56 of 122 participants] vs 56.0% [56 of 100 participants], respectively; P = .14) and positive-report rates (2.3% [122 of 5238 participants] vs 1.9% [100 of 5238 participants]; P = .14).

evidence.title: Conventional Versus Artificial Intelligence-Assisted Interpretation of Chest Radiographs in Patients With Acute Respiratory Symptoms in Emergency Department: A Pragmatic Randomized Clinical Trial
evidence.outcome: Human-plus-AI vs human-only radiologist performance in the intended deployment mode
evidence.effect: Radiologists with AI-CAD had sensitivity 67.2% vs 66.0% without and false-positive rate 19.3% vs 18.5%; no significant differences (P=0.917, P=0.985).
evidence.quote: The sensitivity (67.2% [317/472] in the intervention group vs. 66.0% [324/491] in the control group; odds ratio, 1.02 [95% confidence interval, 0.70-1.49]; P = 0.917) and false-positive rate (19.3% [249/1289] vs. 18.5% [245/1324]; odds ratio, 1.00 [95% confidence interval, 0.79-1.26]; P = 0.985) of CR interpretation by duty radiologists were not associated with the use of AI-CAD.

evidence.title: Effect of an artificial intelligence-assisted system on endoscopic diagnosis of superficial oesophageal squamous cell carcinoma and precancerous lesions: a multicentre, tandem, double-blind, randomised controlled trial
evidence.outcome: Clinician performance (lesion miss rate) with versus without AI assistance in intended deployment mode
evidence.effect: Endoscopists with AI had lower point-estimate miss rates (per-lesion 1.7% vs 6.7%), but confidence intervals were wide and not statistically significant (p=0.079).
evidence.quote: The observed effect of AI-assisted endoscopy on the per-lesion and per-patient miss rates of superficial oesophageal squamous cell carcinoma and precancerous lesions under WLE and non-magnified NBI was consistent with substantial benefit through to a neutral or small negative effect.

evidence.title: A deep-learning model for intracranial aneurysm detection on CT angiography images in China: a stepwise, multicentre, early-stage clinical validation study
evidence.outcome: clinician diagnostic performance
evidence.effect: AI-assisted strategy improved clinicians' diagnostic AUC from 0.795 to 0.878 on a per-patient basis.
evidence.quote: In the multi-reader multi-case study, the AI-assisted strategy improved clinicians' diagnostic performance both on a per-patient basis (the area under the receiver operating characteristic curves [AUCs]; 0·795 [0·761-0·830] without AI vs 0·878 [0·850-0·906] with AI; p<0·0001) and a per-aneurysm basis (the area under the weighted alternative free-response receiver operating characteristic curves; 0·765 [0·732-0·799] vs 0·865 [0·839-0·891]; p<0·0001).

evidence.title: An eyecare foundation model for clinical assistance: a randomized controlled trial
evidence.outcome: Ophthalmologist diagnostic performance with versus without AI copilot in intended deployment mode
evidence.effect: Ophthalmologists with EyeFM copilot had higher correct diagnostic rate (92.2% vs 75.4%, P<0.001) than standard care; overreliance not reported in the abstract.
evidence.quote: The primary endpoint indicated that ophthalmologists with EyeFM copilot achieved higher correct diagnostic rate (92.2% versus 75.4%, P < 0.001) and referral rate (92.2% versus 80.5%, P < 0.001).

evidence.title: Artificial Intelligence-Based Automated Echocardiographic Analysis and the Workflow of Sonographers: A Randomized Crossover Trial (AI-Echo RCT)
evidence.venue: Journal of the American Heart Association
evidence.outcome: Sonographer workflow efficiency, fatigue and image quality with versus without AI assistance in a randomized crossover trial
evidence.effect: AI days vs non-AI days: exam time 13.0±3.5 vs 14.3±4.2 min (P<0.001); daily exams 16.7±2.5 vs 14.1±2.5 (P=0.003); mental fatigue 4.1±1.1 vs 4.7±0.6 (P=0.039).
evidence.quote: This real-world randomized trial demonstrated that AI-based echocardiographic analysis enhances workflow efficiency, reduces sonographer fatigue, and improves image quality without compromising diagnostic integrity.

evidence.title: Interval cancer, sensitivity, and specificity comparing AI-supported mammography screening with standard double reading without AI in the MASAI study: a randomised, controlled, non-inferiority, single-blinded, population-based, screening-accuracy trial
evidence.outcome: Screening sensitivity with AI-supported radiologist reading versus standard double reading
evidence.effect: Sensitivity was 80·5% [95% CI 76·4-84·2] with AI versus 73·8% [68·9-78·3] without AI (p=0·031), consistent across age and breast density.
evidence.quote: Sensitivity was higher in the intervention group (80·5% [95% CI 76·4-84·2]) than the control group (73·8% [68·9-78·3]; p=0·031), an effect consistent across age and breast density, and for invasive cancer but not for in-situ cancer.

evidence.title: Evaluating AI-assisted detection of fetal intracranial malformations in prenatal ultrasound practice: a multicentre, self-crossover, randomised controlled trial in China
evidence.outcome: Human-AI team performance compared with sonographers without AI in intended deployment mode
evidence.effect: Malformation-targeted sensitivity improved by 0·118 (95% CI 0·054 to 0·181; p superiority<0·0001); specificity non-inferior (difference 0·001, 95% CI -0·001 to 0·002).
evidence.quote: In the malformation-targeted analysis, sensitivity improved by 0·118 (95% CI 0·054 to 0·181; p<sub>superiority</sub><0·0001), and specificity was also non-inferior (difference 0·001, 95% CI -0·001 to 0·002; p<sub>non-inferiority</sub><0·0001).

evidence.title: A clinical-grade universal foundation model for intraoperative pathology
evidence.outcome: Human-AI collaboration effect on pathologist diagnostic workload and micrometastasis detection
evidence.effect: Human-AI collaboration reduced diagnostic workload by 35%, avoided 105 ancillary tests, and enhanced micrometastasis detection with 87.5% accuracy.
evidence.quote: Human-AI collaboration further reduced diagnostic workload by 35%, avoided 105 ancillary tests and enhanced detection of micrometastases with 87.5% accuracy.

evidence.title: Does LLM Assistance Improve Healthcare Delivery? An Evaluation Using On-site Physicians and Laboratory Tests∗
evidence.outcome: Diagnostic alignment and treatment decisions in health-worker plans with versus without LLM feedback, judged by on-site physicians
evidence.effect: Health workers changed prescribing for more than half of patients, but on-site physicians saw little to no improvement; lab tests showed mixed effects with no significant increase in detection rates.
evidence.quote: However, on-site physicians observed little to no improvement in diagnostic alignment or treatment decisions.

evidence.title: Prospective Clinical Evaluation of a Deep Learning Algorithm for Guided Point-of-Care Ultrasonography Screening of Abdominal Aortic Aneurysms
evidence.outcome: Scan quality of DL-guided novice nurses versus physicians without DL guidance
evidence.effect: DL-guided novices achieved adequate scan quality in 87.5% (95% CI 82.7-92.3%) of patients, comparable to 91.3% (87.2-95.4%) for physicians (p=0.310).
evidence.quote: The DL-guided novices achieved adequate scan quality in 87.5% (95% CI: 82.7 - 92.3%) of patients, comparable to the 91.3% (95% CI: 87.2-95.4%) rate of physician scans (p=0.310).

evidence.title: Clinical value of artificial intelligence in thyroid ultrasound: a prospective study from the real world
evidence.outcome: Reader diagnostic performance with versus without AI reports for thyroid nodules
evidence.effect: AI-assisted residents significantly improved accuracy and sensitivity for nodules ≤ 1.5 cm (all p < 0.01) and reduced unnecessary biopsy rate by up to 27.7% for nodules > 1.5 cm (p = 0.034).
evidence.quote: The AI-assisted resident strategy significantly improved the accuracy and sensitivity for nodules ≤ 1.5 cm (all p < 0.01), while reducing the unnecessary biopsy rate by up to 27.7% for nodules > 1.5 cm (p = 0.034).

evidence.title: Development, Deployment, and Implementation of a Machine Learning Surgical Case Length Prediction Model and Prospective Evaluation
evidence.outcome: Scheduler case-length prediction accuracy with versus without model assistance in live deployment
evidence.effect: Model-assisted schedulers predicted 3.4% more cases within 20% of actual length and 4.3% fewer underpredicted cases; the model alone did better still (5.9% more within 20%, 11.2% fewer underpredicted) than schedulers alone.
evidence.quote: The model assisted schedulers to predict 3.4% more cases within 20% of the actual case length and 4.3% fewer underpredicted cases.

evidence.title: Prospective implementation of AI-assisted screen reading to improve early detection of breast cancer
evidence.outcome: cancer detection and recalls
evidence.effect: Comparing human readers with and without the AI assistant demonstrated a 7% relative increase in cancer detection rate (24 more cases) and a 3% relative increase in PPV.
evidence.quote: Across the three phases, the implementation of the AI-assisted additional-reader workflow resulted in 24 more cancer cases detected (7% relative increase in cancer detection rate (CDR)) and 70 more women recalled (0.28% increase in absolute recall rate), at a positive predictive value (PPV) for screening of 20.0% (3% relative increase) (Table 3 ).

evidence.title: Artificial Intelligence-Assisted Prescription Determination for Orthokeratology Lens Fitting: From Algorithm to Clinical Practice
evidence.outcome: Number of trials to final prescription with vs without AI assistance among clinicians
evidence.effect: Trials needed decreased significantly for six of seven clinicians (all P<0.01); reduction larger for junior than senior clinicians (0.76±0.60 vs 0.32±0.60, P<0.001). Junior and senior clinicians had comparable outcomes (93.96% vs 94.44%, P=0.864).
evidence.quote: With the assistance of the AI system, the number of trials required to determine the final prescription significantly decreased for six of the seven participating clinicians (all P <0.01).
evidence.sample_unit: eyes fitted (real-world trial); 11,502 lens fitting records for algorithm development

evidence.title: Prospective Evaluation of Artificial Intelligence Triage of Incidental Pulmonary Emboli on Contrast-Enhanced CT Examinations of the Chest or Abdomen
evidence.outcome: sensitivity and specificity
evidence.effect: Sensitivity was 80.0% without AI vs 96.2% with AI (p=.03), with no significant difference in specificity.
evidence.quote: Radiologists without AI, in comparison to radiologists with AI, showed significantly lower sensitivity (80.0% vs 96.2%, respectively; p = .03), without a significant difference in specificity (99.9% vs 99.9%, p = .58), for the detection of IPE.

evidence.title: Comparing Clinician Estimates versus a Statistical Tool for Predicting Risk of Death within 45 Days of Admission for Cancer Patients
evidence.outcome: Discrimination (AUC) of clinicians alone, model alone, and clinicians combined with model
evidence.effect: Model AUC 0.834 vs clinicians 0.753 (p<0.0001); integrating clinician predictions with model raised AUC to 0.853 (p<0.0001).
evidence.quote: Integrating clinician predictions with the model's estimates further increased the AUC to 0.853 (p < 0.0001).

evidence.title: Clinical implementation of artificial-intelligence-assisted detection of breast cancer metastases in sentinel lymph nodes: the CONFIDENT-B single-center, non-randomized clinical trial
evidence.outcome: Pathologist sensitivity with versus without AI assistance in clinical workflow
evidence.effect: Micrometastasis sensitivity was 80% for AI-assisted pathologists versus 50% for unassisted pathologists.
evidence.quote: Furthermore, both the sensitivity and the NPVs of AI-assisted pathologists were higher for all types of SN metastases, yet again most strikingly for micrometastases (80% for AI-assisted pathologists versus 50% for unassisted pathologists).

evidence.title: Integrated image-based deep learning and language models for primary diabetes care
evidence.outcome: Referable DR identification accuracy of PCPs with vs without AI assistance
evidence.effect: Average PCP accuracy for identifying referable DR was 81.0% unassisted and 92.3% assisted by DeepDR-Transformer.
evidence.quote: For identifying referable DR, the average PCP's accuracy was 81.0% unassisted and 92.3% assisted by DeepDR-Transformer.
evidence.sample_unit: patients (397 unassisted PCP arm; 372 PCP+DeepDR-LLM arm)

evidence.title: Deep Learning-Driven Glaucoma Medication Bottle Recognition: A Multilingual Clinical Validation Study in Patients with Impaired Vision
evidence.outcome: Medication identification accuracy and time with versus without the AI app, in the same patients
evidence.effect: Accuracy rose from 27.6% without the app to 99.2% with it (OR 319.353, P<0.001), with no significant change in identification time.
evidence.quote: Identification accuracy significantly improved from 27.6% without the app to 99.2% with the app across all participants, with no significant change in identification time.

evidence.title: Real-World Diagnostic Performance and Clinical Utility of Artificial Intelligence-Assisted Interpretation for Detection of Lung Metastasis on CT in Patients With Colorectal Cancer
evidence.outcome: Radiologist-with-AI vs conventional reading performance, and stand-alone AI performance
evidence.effect: AI-assisted sensitivity 72.4% vs 32.1% conventional (p=.008); accuracy 98.5% vs 96.0%. Stand-alone AI had 381 false positives in 634 patients, but radiologists reported only one, so team performance exceeded stand-alone AI.
evidence.quote: The AI-assisted interpretation group compared with the conventional interpretation group showed higher sensitivity (72.4% vs 32.1%, respectively; p = .008), accuracy (98.5% vs 96.0%, p = .005), and frequency of management changes (55.2% vs 25.0%, p = .02), without significant difference in specificity (99.7% vs 98.9%, p = .11), diagnostic yield (3.2% vs 1.4%, p = .30), or false-referral rate (0.3% vs 1.1%, p = .10).

evidence.title: Impact of a computed tomography-based artificial intelligence software on radiologists' workflow for detecting acute intracranial hemorrhage
evidence.outcome: Radiologist diagnostic performance with vs without AI assistance
evidence.effect: No significant differences in accuracy (0.99 to 0.99, P=0.343), sensitivity (1.00 to 1.00, P=0.859), or specificity (1.00 to 0.99, P=0.252) after AI implementation.
evidence.quote: There were no significant differences in accuracy [from 0.99 (95% confidence interval: 0.99-1.00) to 0.99 (0.98-1.00), P = 0.343], sensitivity [from 1.00 (0.99-1.00) to 1.00 (0.99-1.00), P = 0.859], or specificity [from 1.00 (0.99-1.00) to 0.99 (0.97-1.00), P = 0.252] following the implementation of the AI software.

evidence.title: Implementation and clinical evaluation of an in-house thoracic auto-segmentation model for 0.35 T magnetic resonance imaging guided radiotherapy
evidence.venue: Physics and imaging in radiation oncology
evidence.outcome: Contouring time with AI-assisted correction versus manual contouring
evidence.effect: Median total contouring time reduced by 12.6 min (50.3%, p<0.01); significant for lungs and heart, but increases for left bronchial tree (+22.9%), esophagus (+10.3%), trachea (+20.8%).
evidence.quote: Statistically significant median time reductions – based on a p < 0 . 025 threshold – were observed for the right lung (5.7 min, a 90.7% reduction), left lung (5.9 min, a 92.7% reduction), heart (1.1 min, a 52.9% reduction) and total contouring time (12.6 min, a 50.3% reduction).

evidence.title: Computer-Aided Detection Colonoscopy for Surveillance in IBD Patients: Insights from a Single-Center Experience
evidence.outcome: Endoscopist detection performance with versus without AI assistance in intended deployment mode
evidence.effect: ADR with CADe 3.8% vs 5.2% without (P = .315); subgroups by experience, IBD type, and timing showed similar nonsignificant declining trend.
evidence.quote: Subgroup analyses stratified by endoscopist experience, IBD type, and procedure timing (daytime vs after hours) corroborated a similar nonsignificant declining trend in ADR after CADe introduction.

evidence.title: Real-world clinical impact of three commercial AI algorithms on musculoskeletal radiography interpretation: A prospective crossover reader study
evidence.outcome: Reader diagnostic performance (AUC) with versus without AI assistance in crossover design
evidence.effect: AI assistance did not significantly change AUC for fractures, dislocations, or effusions (e.g., fractures Reader 1 96.50% vs 96.30-96.50%, all p > 0.11); reading time fell and confidence rose.
evidence.quote: AI assistance did not significantly change performance for fractures, dislocations, or effusions.
evidence.sample_unit: adult musculoskeletal studies (2,926 radiographs) read by 2 radiologists

evidence.title: Deep learning CT model for stratified diagnosis of pancreatic cystic neoplasms: multicenter development, validation, and real-world clinical impact
evidence.outcome: Radiologist diagnostic accuracy with versus without AI assistance in MRMC study
evidence.effect: AI assistance improved radiologists' AUC from 0.786 to 0.845 (p < 0.05), reduced interpretation time by 23.7% (5.28 vs. 4.03 min/case); radiologists accepted AI recommendations in 87.14% of cases.
evidence.quote: A multi-reader, multi-case (MRMC) study demonstrated that AI assistance significantly improved radiologists' diagnostic accuracy (AUC: 0.786 to 0.845; p < 0.05) and reduced interpretation time by 23.7% (5.28 vs. 4.03 minutes/case).

evidence.title: Fully Automatic AI-Based Quantification of LV Mass in Echocardiography: A Multimodality Validation
evidence.outcome: AI vs expert manual echo LV mass measurement accuracy against CT reference
evidence.effect: AI reduced measurement error by ~20% vs expert; AUC for increased LV mass 0.78 vs 0.71 (linear) and 0.84 vs 0.77 (hybrid).
evidence.quote: Diagnostic accuracy for detecting increased LV mass was higher with AI echocardiography than with Expert echocardiography (AUC: 0.78 vs 0.71 for linear; 0.84 vs 0.77 for hybrid).

evidence.title: Evaluation of computer-aided detection for gastric cancer using white-light and linked-color imaging: a pilot study
evidence.outcome: gastric cancer detection rate
evidence.effect: The GC detection rate was 4.8% in the CADe group versus 1.8% in the control group (difference of 3.0%), which was not statistically significant (p=0.07).
evidence.quote: The GC detection rate in the CADe group was slightly higher than in the control group (difference, 3.0%; 95% CI, 0.3%-6.3%), although the difference was not statistically significant ( P = .07).

evidence.title: Real-world use of PACS-integrated automated spine numbering in MRI
evidence.outcome: Reading time with vs without AI labeling by radiologist type
evidence.effect: Reading times were reduced for residents (p < 0.05) but not for specialists; overall reading times did not differ significantly (p = 0.0858).
evidence.quote: Integrating an AI-assisted spine labeling algorithm into the PACS significantly reduced reading times for residents (p < 0.05) but not for specialists.

evidence.title: Computer-Aided Colonoscopy Alert Fatigue and Its Effect on Adenoma Detection
evidence.outcome: Performance of endoscopists with versus without AI in deployment, assessing reliance/fatigue
evidence.effect: Early CADe ADR 49.9% vs 39.4% unassisted; late CADe ADR 39.9% vs 40.9% unassisted, suggesting diminished responsiveness to CADe.
evidence.quote: By contrast, ADR in CADe-assisted procedures was markedly higher in the first 3 procedures (49.9%, 95% CI [45.5-54.3]) but dropped significantly to 39.9% (95% CI [33.8-46.3]) in later procedures.

evidence.title: Real-Time Integration of an AI-Based ECG Interpretation System in the Emergency Department: A Pragmatic Alternating-Day Study of Diagnostic Performance and Clinical Process Metrics
evidence.outcome: STEMI sensitivity and reperfusion time metrics on AI-disclosure days versus physician-only days
evidence.effect: AI sensitivity 96.7% vs physician 68.3% (p=0.027); specificity 75.9% vs 84.5%; door-to-balloon 40.0 vs 47.34 min (p=0.001); mortality 17.0% vs 16.77% (p=0.191)
evidence.quote: Real-time AI-ECG integration in the ED was associated with improved STEMI detection sensitivity and shorter reperfusion-related time metrics, particularly in atypical presentations, and with reduced hospital LOS among admitted patients.

evidence.title: Hybrid supervised deep learning for lung adenocarcinoma diagnosis to optimize surgical strategies
evidence.outcome: Pathologist diagnostic accuracy with vs without AI invasive-lesion prompts
evidence.effect: Reader study (3 pathologists, n=137 WSIs): accuracy gains 11.7%, 28.5%, 28.5%; panel AUC 0.616 to 0.921. Prospective 70 patients: 82.86% manual vs 92.9% with AI; 5 surgical approaches modified.
evidence.quote: The analysis revealed that HSFLA improved the pathologists’ diagnostic AUC from 0.616 to 0.921.

evidence.title: ArcMAP - ML assisted medical concept mapping to accelerate NHS data standardization
evidence.outcome: mapping efficiency
evidence.effect: estimated >2-fold increase in efficiency when using ArcMAP compared to manual sessions
evidence.quote: In contrast, during the manual mapping sessions without ArcMAP, only 31.7 ± 0.9 ( Supplementary Table 2 ) concepts were mapped on average, resulting in an estimated >2-fold increase in efficiency when using ArcMAP.
evidence.sample_unit: source concepts (6,179 medication names and 2,261 laboratory test names)

evidence.title: A non-invasive end-to-end intelligent assistance system for breast ultrasound
evidence.outcome: Radiologist diagnostic accuracy with versus without BIRD assistance in reader studies
evidence.effect: BIRD significantly improved radiologists' accuracy in 2 reader studies (P < 0.05); internal test accuracy 0.837 (95% CI 0.827-0.846).
evidence.quote: The accuracy of BIRD in the internal test set is 0.837 (95% confidence interval: 0.827-0.846), which significantly improves radiologists' accuracy in 2 reader studies (P < 0.05).

evidence.title: Influence of Artificial Intelligence Assistance on Gleason Grading and Prostate Cancer Detection by Uropathologists in Daily Practice: A Prospective Multicenter Study
evidence.outcome: AI-assisted versus unassisted grade-group assessments and tumor detection agreement
evidence.effect: GG assessments differed in 16.5% (30/182); 36.7% (11/30) of discrepancies shifted between GG1 and GG2. Tumor detection agreement was 98.6% (279/283), with differences limited to GG1 tumors.
evidence.quote: GG assessments differed in 16.5% (30/182) of entries when comparing AI-assisted with unassisted evaluations.

evidence.title: Fracture Detection on Bone Radiographs: The Impact of an AI Tool on Orthopaedic Night Shifts
evidence.outcome: Orthopaedist fracture misdiagnosis with versus without AI assistance in deployed setting
evidence.effect: Missed fractures 16 pre-implementation vs 13 post; fracture-related recall rate 0.19% vs 0.17% (p=0.63), non-significant.
evidence.quote: Statistical analyses measured the rates of fracture misdiagnosis before and after implementation of Gleamer BoneView<sup>®</sup>.

evidence.title: Artificial intelligence for pediatric fracture detection: impact on diagnostic revisions and patient recall rates in a tertiary emergency setting
evidence.outcome: Clinician performance and workflow outcomes with vs without AI assistance in the intended deployment mode
evidence.effect: Senior consultation 14.3% vs 12.5%, length of stay 2.3 h vs 2.4 h, and subjective diagnostic confidence showed no significant differences with AI.
evidence.quote: No significant differences were observed for secondary endpoints, including need for senior consultation (14.3% vs. 12.5%), subjective diagnostic confidence, or length of stay (2.3 h vs. 2.4 h).

evidence.title: Artificial Intelligence-Assisted Chest Radiography: A Prospective Crossover Multi-Reader Study on Diagnostic Performance and Workflow Efficiency
evidence.outcome: Reader diagnostic accuracy with versus without AI assistance in intended deployment mode
evidence.effect: AI assistance did not improve diagnostic accuracy; for pleural effusions and pulmonary nodules accuracy decreased in several reader-tool pairings due to increased false positives.
evidence.quote: AI assistance did not improve diagnostic accuracy.
evidence.sample_unit: patients (1861 radiographs) read by five readers

evidence.title: Prospective multi-centre evaluation of guideline-based artificial intelligence to streamline multidisciplinary tumour board
evidence.outcome: change in diagnosis and treatment plan
evidence.effect: Evaluating clinicians with and without AI showed that the combination of human tumor boards with AI reduced subsequent plan changes to 14.73% compared to 28.08% for humans alone.
evidence.quote: The combination of the MTB with AI gives the most effective result in reducing the change in D and TP from 28.08% to 14.73% within 6 months.

evidence.title: A clinically-oriented foundation model for intraoperative pathology
evidence.outcome: Pathologist workload and ancillary tests with versus without AI collaboration
evidence.effect: Human-AI collaboration reduced diagnostic workload by 35%, avoided 105 ancillary tests, and detected micrometastases with 87.5% accuracy.
evidence.quote: Human-AI collaboration further reduced diagnostic workload by 35%, avoided 105 ancillary tests and enhanced detection of micrometastases with 87.5% accuracy.

evidence.title: AI-based delineation based on clinical data in MR-guided brachytherapy for cervical cancer reduces delineation time - A prospective paired trial
evidence.venue: Physica medica : PM : an international journal devoted to the applications of physics to medicine and biology : official journal of the Italian Association of Biomedical Physics (AIFB)
evidence.outcome: Delineation time with versus without AI assistance in intended deployment mode
evidence.effect: AI-assisted delineation reduced time by 10.1 min (95% CI 7.4-12), a 31% decrease compared with oncologist delineating from scratch.
evidence.quote: AI-based delineations resulted in a time reduction of 10.1 min (95% CI: [7.4, 12] minutes), corresponding to a 31% decrease in delineation time.

evidence.title: Artificial intelligence guided physician directive improves head and neck planning quality and practice Uniformity: A prospective study
evidence.outcome: plan achievability with vs without AI
evidence.effect: Plan achievability increased significantly from 52.9% before AI guidance to 80.4% after AI guidance.
evidence.quote: As seen in Fig. 4 a, there is a significant increase in plan achievability pre- and post-AI guidance, from 52.9% to 80.4%.

evidence.title: Artificial intelligence in mobile health for skin cancer diagnostics at home (AIM HIGH): a pilot feasibility study
evidence.outcome: GP diagnosis and treatment plan changes when blinded versus unblinded to AI app assessment
evidence.effect: GPs never changed their working diagnosis but changed their treatment plan in 5 patients based on the app's assessments; 45 of 50 GP assessments completed successfully.
evidence.quote: GPs never changed their working diagnosis, but did change their treatment plan (n = 5) based on the app's assessments.

evidence.title: Human factors in the clinical implementation of deep learning-based automated contouring of pelvic organs at risk for MRI-guided radiotherapy
evidence.outcome: Expert-consensus vs clinically used contour agreement (DSC) and dose differences before vs after auto-contouring
evidence.effect: Contouring behavior changed after automation. Femoral head DSC vs expert consensus rose from 0.91 to 0.93 and rectum fell from 0.88 to 0.85. Max-dose differences were not statistically significant.
evidence.quote: Automation bias was observed, but it had little deleterious effect on treatment planning.

evidence.title: Deep learning-based automatic ASPECTS calculation can improve diagnosis efficiency in patients with acute ischemic stroke: a multicenter study
evidence.outcome: Physician ASPECTS diagnostic AUC and reading time with versus without the AI system
evidence.effect: Combining the system with physicians improved AUC from 67.43% to 89.76% and reduced diagnosis time from 130.6 ± 66.3 s to 33.3 ± 8.3 s (p < 0.001).
evidence.quote: Combining the system with physicians improved AUC from 67.43 to 89.76%, reducing diagnosis time from 130.6 ± 66.3 s to 33.3 ± 8.3 s (p < 0.001).
evidence.sample_unit: NCCT scans (retrospective, four centers); plus 13,399 patients in prospective application

evidence.title: Improving diabetic retinopathy screening using artificial intelligence: design, evaluation and before-and-after study of a custom development
evidence.outcome: GP screening sensitivity and agreement with AI in deployed workflow, before versus after AI
evidence.effect: NaIA-RD influenced screening criteria of 3/4 GPs, increasing their sensitivity. Agreement with GPs was 94.6% or more for non-referral proposals but 23.4% to 86.6% for referral proposals.
evidence.quote: NaIA-RD influenced the screening criteria of 3/4 GPs, increasing their sensitivity.
evidence.sample_unit: patients screened (19,828 before and 22,962 after NaIA-RD implementation)

evidence.title: Effectiveness of Artificial Intelligence-Assisted Colposcopy in a Resource-Limited Population
evidence.outcome: Sensitivity for CIN 2+ with conventional colposcopy vs AI alone vs AI-assisted colposcopy
evidence.effect: CIN 2+ sensitivity was 96.0% for AI colposcopy and 100% for AI-assisted colposcopy vs 85.9% for conventional colposcopy (P=.026, P<.001). AI flagged 77.6% of women as positive vs 47.5% conventionally.
evidence.quote: The sensitivity for detecting CIN 2+ was significantly higher for AI colposcopy (96.0%) and AI-assisted colposcopy (100%) than for conventional colposcopy (85.9%, P =.026, P <.001, respectively).

evidence.title: Left Ventricular Ejection Fraction Reporting Variability and AI-Assisted Reproducibility: A Multicentre Analysis
evidence.outcome: Reproducibility and time of AI-assisted versus fully manual LVEF analysis by operators
evidence.effect: AI-assisted mode reduced assessment time; interobserver ICCs 0.968, 0.974, 0.984 vs 0.913, 0.924, 0.971 manual; CV 2.5%, 3.8%, 4.4% vs 5.6%, 8.8%, 9.3%.
evidence.quote: The AI-assisted method not only significantly reduced LVEF assessment time compared with manual analysis, but also showed superior reproducibility.

evidence.title: Automated assessment of right ventricular systolic function from coronary angiograms with video-based artificial intelligence algorithms: development, validation, comparison against humans, and prospective deployment
evidence.outcome: Clinician and student accuracy identifying reduced RVSF with versus without AI assistance
evidence.effect: AI assistance improved accuracy for cardiologists (72.1-77.6%) and medical students (43.5-64.0%); AI alone reached 79.5% accuracy; cardiologists with AI had highest specificity (84.6%).
evidence.quote: In a human performance evaluation (n = 200), artificial intelligence (AI) assistance improved accuracy of identifying RVSF for cardiologists (72.1-77.6%) and medical students (43.5-64.0%).
evidence.sample_unit: coronary angiography studies (development set; also 2247 UCSF external studies, 82 prospective STEMI cases, 200 human-evaluation cases)

evidence.title: Development and Implementation of an AI System for Generating Clinical Urine Drug Test Sign-Outs
evidence.outcome: Clinical sign-out time with versus without AI-generated preliminary sign-outs in the workflow
evidence.effect: Sign-out time fell by 28.5 seconds per case (23% efficiency gain), and by 65 seconds per case (51%) with a second non-AI workflow improvement. Overreliance was not assessed.
evidence.quote: Workflow integration of the AI tool reduced clinical sign-out times by 28.5 seconds per case (23% efficiency gain), and by 65 seconds per case (51% efficiency gain) when integrated alongside a second, non-AI workflow improvement.

evidence.title: Artificial Intelligence-Based CTA Software for Real-World Detection of Large-Vessel Occlusion in Acute Ischemic Stroke
evidence.outcome: Time to diagnostic conclusion with versus without AI assistance across reader experience levels
evidence.effect: AI assistance significantly reduced time to diagnostic conclusion across all reader profiles.
evidence.quote: AI assistance significantly reduced time to diagnostic conclusion across all reader profiles.

evidence.title: First, do NOHARM: a medical safety benchmark and randomized study of physician and AI teaming on clinical consultations
evidence.outcome: Physician performance with AI assistance versus conventional resources; omission of AI-generated recommendations
evidence.effect: In a randomized study of 101 physicians, AI assistance improved performance compared to conventional resources, but AI-assisted physicians frequently omitted valuable AI recommendations and still scored lower than many AI systems alone.
evidence.quote: In a randomized study of 101 U.S.-licensed generalist physicians, AI assistance improved physician performance compared to conventional resources.

evidence.title: Automated Healthcare Thematic Analysis using Multi-Agent Large Language Model: Algorithm Development and Evaluation
evidence.outcome: Junior investigators working with CoTI versus CoTI alone; possible overreliance
evidence.effect: Human-AI collaboration between CoTI and junior investigators gave only marginal gains compared to CoTI alone; junior investigators may over-rely on CoTI (hypothesis).
evidence.quote: In an exploratory human-AI collaboration experiment, we found that the collaboration between CoTI and junior investigators provided only marginal gains compared to CoTI alone.

evidence.title: Human-AI Co-reasoning for Clinical Diagnosis with Evidence-Integrated Language Agent
evidence.outcome: Physician diagnostic performance with versus without AI assistance, including automation bias
evidence.effect: PULSE assistance enabled physicians to correct initial errors and broaden diagnostic hypotheses, but also introduced risks of automation bias; serial and concurrent workflows were explored.
evidence.quote: When used collaboratively, PULSE enabled physicians to correct initial errors and broaden diagnostic hypotheses, but also introduced risks of automation bias.

evidence.title: Deliberative multi-agent large language models improve clinical reasoning in ophthalmology
evidence.outcome: Diagnostic accuracy of multi-agent councils vs pooled individual LLMs on ophthalmology vignettes
evidence.effect: Councils outperformed pooled individual models in all tiers. Accuracy was 95.0% vs 90.8% (flagship), 96.0% vs 86.5% (fast), and 91.0% vs 83.2% (open-source).
evidence.quote: Accuracy improved for proprietary flagship (95.0% vs 90.8%; risk difference [RD]: 4.25 [95% CI: 0.45, 8.05]), proprietary fast (96.0% vs 86.5%; RD: 9.50 [5.31, 13.59]), and open-source councils (91.0% vs 83.2%; RD: 7.75 [4.17, 11.33]).

evidence.title: AD-CARE: A Guideline-grounded, Modality-agnostic LLM Agent for Real-world Alzheimer's Disease Diagnosis with Multi-cohort Assessment, Fairness Analysis, and Reader Study
evidence.outcome: Neurologist and radiologist diagnostic accuracy and decision time with versus without the AI agent
evidence.effect: Agent improved neurologist and radiologist accuracy by 6%-11% and more than halved decision time in a controlled reader study; overreliance not reported in the abstract.
evidence.quote: In a controlled reader study, the agent improved neurologist and radiologist accuracy by 6%-11% and more than halved decision time.

evidence.title: Resolving the bias-precision paradox with stochastic causal representation learning for personalized medicine
evidence.outcome: Clinician decision accuracy and decision time with versus without AI support
evidence.effect: Clinician accuracy improved by 14.7% while decision time was reduced with the AI method.
evidence.quote: In human-AI evaluation, our method outperforms clinicians-in-training and large language models, and improves clinician accuracy by 14.7% while reducing decision time, enabling interpretable, real-time clinical decision support.

evidence.title: A specialized reasoning large language model for accelerating rare disease diagnosis: a randomized AI physician assistance trial
evidence.outcome: Physician rare-disease diagnostic accuracy with LLM assistance versus internet search alone
evidence.effect: RaDaR assistance improved physicians' rare-disease diagnostic accuracy by 21.44 percentage points compared with internet search alone.
evidence.quote: In a randomized physician-assistance trial, RaDaR assistance improved physicians' rare-disease diagnostic accuracy by 21.44 percentage points compared with internet search alone.

evidence.title: Towards Precision Therapy in Hepatocellular Carcinoma: A Clinical-Reasoning LLM for Risk Stratification and Treatment Guidance
evidence.outcome: Physician decision accuracy and speed with versus without the LLM assistant
evidence.effect: Physicians using HCC-STAR as an assistant made more accurate decisions faster; the model also surpassed resident and attending physicians in treatment accuracy. No numbers in abstract.
evidence.quote: The model surpassed resident and attending physicians in treatment accuracy and helped physicians make more accurate decisions faster when used as an assistant.

evidence.title: Human-in-the-Loop Large Language Model Framework for Identification of Cutaneous Immune-Related Adverse Events
evidence.outcome: Reviewer accuracy, agreement and review time with versus without LLM assistance
evidence.effect: LLM-assisted workflow improved accuracy (F1 = 0.88 vs 0.77), Cohen's kappa (0.82 vs 0.50), and reduced average review time by approximately half.
evidence.quote: Compared with unassisted manual review, the LLM-assisted workflow improved accuracy (F1 = 0.88 vs 0.77), inter-rater agreement measured by Cohen's kappa (kappa = 0.82 vs 0.50), and reduced average review time by approximately half.

evidence.title: RareLens: Towards End-to-End Rare Disease Care via Aligning Divergent Large Language Model Reasoning
evidence.outcome: Physician performance with versus without AI assistance, compared with autonomous AI
evidence.effect: Autonomous RareLens and physicians assisted by RareLens both outperformed unaided physicians; effective human-AI collaboration required more than simply providing model outputs.
evidence.quote: In an external evaluation involving 1,287 cases and 23 physicians, autonomous RareLens and physicians assisted by RareLens both outperformed unaided physicians, while demonstrating that effective human-AI collaboration requires more than simply providing model outputs.

evidence.title: Large language models improve physician accuracy but lead to false reliance
evidence.outcome: Physician accuracy with versus without LLM assistance and reliance on the AI
evidence.effect: Physician accuracy increased from 70.8% unaided to 82.6% with CORA; resistance to incorrect LLM answers fell from 92% to 34.8% when the answer appeared citation-supported.
evidence.quote: In a study of 46 physicians, accuracy increased from 70.8% unaided to 82.6% with CORA.

evidence.title: Grounding Large Language Model in Clinical Diagnostics
evidence.outcome: Diagnostic accuracy and efficiency of ClinDiag-GPT plus physicians versus physicians alone
evidence.effect: Collaboration between ClinDiag-GPT and physicians enhanced both diagnostic accuracy and efficiency compared with physicians alone and the model alone.
evidence.quote: Collaboration between ClinDiag-GPT and physicians enhanced both diagnostic accuracy and efficiency, demonstrating ClinDiag-GPT's potential as a valuable clinical assistant.

evidence.title: AI-literacy training enhances physician-LLM diagnostic collaboration in a resource-limited setting: a randomized controlled trial
evidence.outcome: Diagnostic reasoning score for physicians with vs without LLM access, plus LLM alone comparison
evidence.effect: Physician+LLM 71.4% vs 42.6% conventional resources; adjusted difference 27.5 pp (95% CI 22.8 to 32.2). LLM alone outperformed physician+LLM by 11.5 pp.
evidence.quote: Of 58 physicians completing the study, those with LLM access achieved mean diagnostic reasoning scores of 71.4% versus 42.6% with conventional medical resources alone, yielding an adjusted difference of 27.5 percentage points (95% CI, 22.8 to 32.2; P < 0.001).

evidence.title: From Tool to Teammate: A Randomized Controlled Trial of Clinician-AI Collaborative Workflows for Diagnosis
evidence.outcome: Diagnostic accuracy of clinicians with collaborative AI workflows versus traditional resources
evidence.effect: Clinicians using collaborative workflows achieved 85% (AI-first) and 82% (AI-second) accuracy versus 75% with traditional resources (p < 0.0004 and p < 0.00001); no significant difference from AI-alone at 90%.
evidence.quote: Clinicians using either collaborative workflow outperformed those using traditional tools, achieving average accuracies of 85% (AI-first) and 82% (AI-second), compared to 75% with traditional resources (p < 0.0004 and p < 0.00001; mean differences = 9.8% and 6.8%; 95% CI = 4.6%–15% and 4.0%–9.6%).

evidence.title: Impact of LLM Assistance on Physician Decision-Making: A Multi-Country Randomized Controlled Trial  ∗
evidence.outcome: Physician clinical vignette performance with vs without GPT-4o access
evidence.effect: LLM access improved performance: Kenya 18% (95% CI 12.7 to 23.2), Indonesia 10.7% (5.7 to 15.7), Netherlands 7.2% (3.7 to 10.7), all p<0.001; some physicians without access outperformed those with access.
evidence.quote: Results showed that LLM access significantly improved clinical performance, with the largest effect in Kenya (18%, 95% CI: 12.7 to 23.2, p  < 0.001), followed by Indonesia (10.7%, 95% CI: 5.7 to 15.7, p  < 0.001) and the Netherlands (7.2%, 95% CI: 3.7 to 10.7, p  < 0.001).

evidence.title: Artificial Intelligence and Dental Professionals’ Performance in the Identification of Dental Implant Systems: The Impact of Deep Learning Algorithms – A Diagnostic Accuracy Study
evidence.outcome: Dental professionals' implant identification performance with versus without AI assistance, compared with standalone AI
evidence.effect: AI assistance significantly improved all metrics across all implant groups (p<0.05) except recall of NucleOSS T4, but assisted performance stayed below standalone AI, indicating automation bias.
evidence.quote: AI assistance improved participants’ diagnostic performance across all implant categories but did not exceed the standalone AI model, underscoring the impact of human–AI interaction and automation bias.

evidence.title: Artificial Intelligence-assisted reader evaluation in acute CT head interpretation (AI-REACT): a multireader multicase study
evidence.outcome: Reader sensitivity and specificity with versus without AI assistance for critical CT head abnormalities
evidence.effect: Pooled reader sensitivity rose from 82.8% to 89.7% (+6.9%, p<0.001) with AI; specificity fell from 84.5% to 78.9% (-5.5%, p=0.046). ED clinicians with AI matched unaided radiologists' sensitivity.
evidence.quote: With AI assistance, pooled reader sensitivity for critically abnormal scans increased from 82.8% to 89.7% (+6.9%, 95% CI +1.4% to +10.6%, p<0.001), and for intracranial haemorrhage from 84.6% to 91.6% (+7.0%, 95% CI +3.2% to +10.8%, p<0.001), but specificity decreased from 84.5% to 78.9% (–5.5%, 95% CI –11.0% to –0.09%, p=0.046).
evidence.sample_unit: readers (each interpreting 150 NCCTH scans unaided and with AI)

evidence.title: KOM: A Multi-Agent Artificial Intelligence System for Precision Management of Knee Osteoarthritis (KOA)
evidence.outcome: Time and treatment quality for clinician+AI versus clinician alone versus AI alone in randomized simulation
evidence.effect: Clinician-KOM collaboration reduced total diagnostic and planning time by 38.5% and improved treatment quality compared with each approach used independently.
evidence.quote: A randomized three-arm simulation study further revealed that collaboration between KOM and clinicians reduced total diagnostic and planning time by 38.5% and resulted in improved treatment quality compared to each approach used independently.

evidence.title: A hybrid-reasoner LLM framework toward real-world clinical decision- making support in acute ischemic stroke
evidence.outcome: Physician performance with versus without LLM support, by experience level
evidence.effect: Junior and non-specialist physicians benefited most from LLM support, narrowing expertise gaps; no numbers given in the abstract.
evidence.quote: Notably, human–AI interaction experiments revealed that junior and non-specialist physicians benefited most, narrowing expertise gaps.

evidence.title: OphAgent: A Generalisable Ophthalmic Agentic System for Global Eye Care
evidence.outcome: Ophthalmologist diagnostic accuracy with versus without OphAgent assistance in reader study
evidence.effect: OphAgent improved diagnostic accuracy by up to 20% across 14 clinically significant tasks; gains stable across regions, experience levels, and languages.
evidence.quote: In a large-scale global reader study with 311 ophthalmologists from 86 centres across 22 countries, spanning seven languages and settings from tertiary hospitals to resource-limited clinics, OphAgent improved diagnostic accuracy by up to 20% across 14 clinically significant tasks.

evidence.title: Pediatric Autism Diagnosis Accuracy and Confidence: A Comparison of Experienced and Inexperienced Clinicians Making Decisions with and without AI Decision Support
evidence.outcome: Diagnostic accuracy of clinicians with vs without AI support; overreliance assessment
evidence.effect: Accuracy 57.14% with ADIS vs 66.67% without (nonsignificant); trainees 0% accuracy when ADIS wrong vs 68.75% when correct, indicating overreliance.
evidence.quote: Overall diagnostic accuracy was 57.14% when ADIS was active versus 66.67% without ADIS, a nonsignificant difference.

evidence.title: Algorithmic implementation of pancreatic cancer staging guidelines: comparison with a retrieval-augmented large language model
evidence.outcome: Staging accuracy and time for radiologists unassisted vs LLM-assisted vs KBA-assisted
evidence.effect: Accuracy 81.9%, 80.6%, 98.6% (unassisted, LLM-assisted, KBA-assisted); KBA higher than both (p<0.001); staging time 229.2, 401.9, 196.2 s; LLM increased time without improving accuracy.
evidence.quote: In a preliminary comparative experiment, KBA assistance improved staging accuracy without increasing staging time, whereas LLM assistance increased staging time without improving staging accuracy.
evidence.sample_unit: staging assessments (6 radiologists x 12 simulated cases x 1 per condition, per condition 72)

evidence.title: SydneyMTL: Interpretable Multi-Task Learning for Complete Sydney System Assessment in Gastric Biopsies
evidence.outcome: Pathologist interpretation time and inter-observer agreement with vs without AI assistance
evidence.effect: Randomized crossover reader study showed AI-assisted review significantly reduced interpretation time and improved inter-observer agreement.
evidence.quote: Finally, a randomized crossover reader study showed that AI-assisted review significantly reduced interpretation time and improved inter-observer agreement, establishing SydneyMTL as a scalable tool for supporting standardized gastric cancer risk stratification.

evidence.title: I3LUNG: Clinical Validation of a Multimodal AI Tool to Support Immunotherapy Decisions in NSCLC
evidence.outcome: Physician prediction accuracy with versus without the explainable AI tool
evidence.effect: Expert and non-expert physicians could improve their prediction with the explainable AI (XAI) tool; no numbers given in the abstract.
evidence.quote: The clinical usability study showed that expert and non-expert physicians could improve their prediction with the explainable AI (XAI) tool.

evidence.title: A foundation-model-powered AI system with post-read alerts and concurrent assistance improves gastric biopsy diagnosis across 29 pathological categories
evidence.outcome: Reader sensitivity for malignancy and metaplasia
evidence.effect: Sensitivity improved for malignancy 92.2% to 94.8%, P = .034; metaplasia 94.2% to 97.4%, P = .013.
evidence.quote: In a prospective reader study with six pathologists, concurrent AI assistance significantly improves sensitivity for malignancy (92.2% to 94.8%,  <italic>P</italic>  = .034) and metaplasia (94.2% to 97.4%,  <italic>P</italic>  = .013).
evidence.sample_unit: pathologists (reader study); 4,679 biopsies in retrospective multi-hospital simulation

evidence.title: UWF-FM: A Foundation Model for Comprehensive Ultra-Widefield Retinal Assessment
evidence.outcome: Clinician sensitivity and specificity with versus without AI assistance in crossover multi-reader study
evidence.effect: AI assistance increased clinician sensitivity with minimal loss of specificity (600 UWF images; four ophthalmologists).
evidence.quote: In a prospectively registered randomized crossover multi-reader study (ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT07651943; 600 UWF images; four ophthalmologists), AI assistance increased clinician sensitivity with minimal loss of specificity.
evidence.sample_unit: UWF images read in randomized crossover multi-reader study (four ophthalmologists)

evidence.title: Harnessing Pathology Foundation Models to Accelerate Lymphoma Diagnosis Through Automated Immunohistochemistry Triage
evidence.outcome: Lymphoma subtype prediction accuracy from morphology, AI versus practicing pathologists in blinded reader study
evidence.effect: HATS outperformed practicing pathologists at predicting lymphoma subtypes from morphology alone (85% vs 65%).
evidence.quote: In a blinded reader study, HATS outperforms practicing pathologists at predicting lymphoma subtypes from morphology alone (85% vs 65%).

evidence.title: Clinical Validation of an AI-Assisted Ultrasound Workflow for Developmental Dysplasia of the Hip Screening: Sequential Assessment According to the Graf Method
evidence.outcome: Clinician accuracy with versus without CAD
evidence.effect: Mean clinician accuracy increased from 72.3% to 90.2%; paired improvement 17.9 percentage points (95% CI, 10.3–25.4; p&lt;0.001).
evidence.quote: Mean clinician accuracy increased from 72.3% to 90.2% with CAD, a paired improvement of 17.9 percentage points (95% CI, 10.3–25.4; p&lt;0.001; Cohen’s dz=1.31); all 15 clinicians improved.
evidence.sample_unit: images assessed by 15 clinicians with and without CAD

evidence.title: Intelligence Preserves The System It Assists
evidence.outcome: Clinician vs standard model vs augmented model accuracy in ICU pressure control, by departure regime
evidence.effect: In high-departure states augmented model 46.9% vs clinician 20.5% and standard model 19.6%; augmented minus clinician +26.3 points (95% CI 9.3-40.2). Weaker in stable states (25.6%).
evidence.quote: In ICU pressure control, the augmented model was weaker in stable states (25.6%) but strongest in departure states (46.9%), compared with the clinician (20.5%) and standard model (19.6%) in that regime; the high-departure advantage survived stay-level clustering (augmented minus clinician +26.3 points, 95% CI 9.3-40.2; augmented minus standard +27.2 points, 95% CI 12.4-41.1).
evidence.sample_unit: states/rows across five retrospective datasets (JIGSAWS, Cholec80, MIMIC-IV, LUMIERE, PhysioNet Sepsis)

evidence.title: Certified large language model-based diagnostic decision support in rheumatology: the ALLIANCE multicentre randomised controlled trial
evidence.outcome: Physician top-1 diagnostic accuracy with vs without LLM decision support, and over-reliance
evidence.effect: Top-1 accuracy rose 22.2% to 33.3% with the LLM and 23.3% to 35.0% in controls; no between-group difference (adjusted OR 0.99, 95% CI 0.45-2.19; p=0.979). Case time 94 vs 206 s.
evidence.quote: Top-1 accuracy increased from 22.2% to 33.3% in the intervention group and from 23.3% to 35.0% in the control group, with no between-group difference in improvement (adjusted OR 0.99, 95% CI 0.45 to 2.19; p=0.979).

evidence.title: MDT-guided language-model reasoning for spinal infection diagnosis
evidence.outcome: Clinician diagnostic accuracy with versus without fixed AI advice in paired reader study
evidence.effect: Accuracy 92.1% with fixed AI advice vs 89.1% without (difference 3.03 percentage points; 95% CI 1.47 to 4.55); 93 incorrect-to-correct and 41 correct-to-incorrect transitions.
evidence.quote: In the reader study, five clinicians made 1,716 matched reader–case–decision assessments; accuracy was 92.1% with fixed AI advice and 89.1% without advice (difference, 3.03 percentage points; fixed-reader case-bootstrap 95% confidence interval, 1.47 to 4.55), with 93 incorrect-to-correct and 41 correct-to-incorrect transitions.

evidence.title: AI facilitated sperm detection in azoospermic samples for use in ICSI
evidence.outcome: Embryologist sperm search time and sperm found with versus without AI aid on an ICSI microscope
evidence.effect: AI-aided embryologist took less time per droplet (98.90±3.19s vs 168.7±7.84s, P<0.0001) and found 1396 sperm vs 1274 without AI, no significant difference in sperm found.
evidence.quote: In cohort 2, the AI-aided embryologist took significantly less time per droplet (98.90±3.19s vs 168.7±7.84s, P<0.0001) and found 1396 sperm, while 1274 were found without AI, although no significant difference was observed.

evidence.title: Artificial intelligence for personalized management of vestibular schwannoma: A clinical implementation study within a multidisciplinary decision making environment
evidence.outcome: Neuroradiologist preparation time and MDM discussion time with versus without AI-generated reports
evidence.effect: Preparation took 2m54s with AI reports vs 2m36s standard per case. Discussion was shorter with AI, 1m15s vs 1m21s per case.
evidence.quote: However, the computer-assisted simulated MDM (CAS-MDM) approach significantly improved MDM efficiency, with shorter discussion times per patient (1m 15s (± 0m and 28s) per case) compared to standard simulated MDM (SS-MDM) (1m 21s (± 0m and 44s) per case).

evidence.title: ChatGPT Influence on Medical Decision-Making, Bias, and Equity: A Randomized Study of Clinicians Evaluating Clinical Vignettes
evidence.outcome: Physician decision accuracy before versus after receiving ChatGPT+ advice on chest pain vignettes
evidence.effect: Pre-post comparison showed a significant improvement in clinical decision-making accuracy after AI assistance (no numeric estimates in the text).
evidence.quote: Results showed that physicians are willing to change their initial clinical impressions given AI assistance, and that this led to a significant improvement in clinical decision-making accuracy in a chest pain evaluation scenario without introducing or exacerbating existing race or gender biases.

evidence.title: Consensus, dissensus and synergy between clinicians and specialist foundation models in radiology report generation
evidence.outcome: Report quality when clinicians collaborate with AI versus AI alone, for reports containing errors
evidence.effect: Assistive clinician-AI collaboration for reports with errors produced a synergistic improvement across all clinical settings.
evidence.quote: For reports that contain errors we develop an assistive setting, the first demonstration of clinician-AI collaboration for radiology report composition, and we observe a synergistic improvement across all clinical settings.
evidence.sample_unit: certified radiologists evaluating AI-generated and human-written chest radiograph reports

evidence.title: Development and Testing of a Novel Large Language Model-Based Clinical Decision Support Systems for Medication Safety in 12 Clinical Specialties
evidence.outcome: Medication error detection: LLM-CDSS alone versus junior pharmacist plus LLM-CDSS co-pilot
evidence.effect: In co-pilot mode, accuracy, recall, and F1 scores were optimized, with notable improvements in detecting severe DRPs.
evidence.quote: This study established that a RAG-LLM based CDSS significantly boosts the accuracy of medication error identification when used alongside junior pharmacists (co-pilot), with notable improvements in detecting severe DRPs.
evidence.sample_unit: prescribing error scenarios embedded in 23 clinical vignettes

evidence.title: Accuracy and Reliability of 3D Cephalometric Landmark Detection with Deep Learning
evidence.outcome: Specialists' landmarking accuracy and speed with versus without AI assistance
evidence.effect: AI assistance improved landmarking proficiency of senior and junior specialists by 15.9% and 28.9%, and sped the process 6 to 9.5 times.
evidence.quote: The implementation of this model significantly improved the landmarking proficiency of senior and junior specialists by 15.9% and 28.9%, respectively, while also accelerating the process by a factor of 6 to 9.5 times.

evidence.title: Multi-modal AI for Opportunistic Screening, Staging and Progression Risk Stratification of Steatotic Liver Disease
evidence.outcome: Radiologist AUC for steatosis detection with versus without AI assistance
evidence.effect: MAOSS significantly improved the overall AUC for radiologists (n = 11) from 0.709 to 0.798 (p < 0.001).
evidence.quote: Notably, MAOSS significantly improved the overall AUC for radiologists (n = 11) from 0.709 to 0.798 (p < 0.001).
evidence.sample_unit: patients in internal and external validation datasets (plus 18,504 real-world patients, 11 radiologists, 1,192 simulated screening patients)

evidence.title: The effect of medical explanations from large language models on diagnostic decisions in radiology
evidence.outcome: Radiologist diagnostic accuracy with vs without LLM support across explanation formats
evidence.effect: Chain-of-thought explanations improved diagnostic accuracy by 12.2% vs control (P=0.001); +7.2% vs standard output (P=0.040); +9.7% vs differential diagnosis (P=0.004).
evidence.quote: The chain-of-thought explanations yielded the best performance, improving the diagnostic accuracy by 12.2% compared to the control condition without LLM support (  P = 0.001).

evidence.title: Multicentre external validation of a commercial artificial intelligence software to analyse chest radiographs in health screening environments with low disease prevalence
evidence.outcome: Reader AUROC with versus without AI assistance, and reading time
evidence.effect: Readers' AUROCs ranged 0.534-0.676 without AI and 0.571-0.688 with AI (all p<0.05); reading time 2.96-10.27 s longer with AI.
evidence.quote: The readers' AUROCs ranged from 0.534-0.676 without AI and 0.571-0.688 with AI (all p values < 0.05).

evidence.title: Automatic mammographic breast density classification in Chinese women: clinical validation of a deep learning model
evidence.outcome: Radiologist inter-reader consistency (kappa, ICC) before versus after DL model assistance; overreliance not assessed
evidence.effect: Two-category K/ICC rose to 0.81, 0.81, 0.80 from 0.73, 0.75, 0.76; four-category rose to 0.81, 0.82, 0.82 from 0.73, 0.79, 0.78. Overreliance was not assessed.
evidence.quote: The consistency within the junior group, the senior group, and among all radiologists improved with the help of the DL model.

evidence.title: Identification of Active Pulmonary Tuberculosis Among Patients With Positive Interferon-Gamma Release Assay Results: Value of a Deep Learning-based Computer-aided Detection System in Different Scenarios of Implementation
evidence.outcome: Radiologist sensitivity and specificity with versus without CAD assistance
evidence.effect: CAD-assisted interpretation had higher sensitivity (81.8% vs. 72.7%; P=0.046) but lower specificity (84.1% vs. 85.7%; P<0.001) than radiologists alone.
evidence.quote: The CAD-assisted interpretation exhibited a higher sensitivity (81.8% vs. 72.7%; P =0.046) but lower specificity than the radiologists' interpretation (84.1% vs. 85.7%; P <0.001).

evidence.title: How smart is artificial intelligence in organs delineation? Testing a CE and FDA-approved Deep-Learning tool using multiple expert contours delineated on planning CT images
evidence.outcome: Contouring time and inter-observer agreement with versus without AI assistance
evidence.effect: Median manual contouring 25.0 min versus 12.3 min for retrieving and editing DL contours (p<0.001); manually adjusted DL contours showed better inter-RO agreement than manual ones.
evidence.quote: The overall time for retrieving VOIs and their modification was 12.3 minutes (1.9-48.8), resulting in statistically significantly lower than that of the manual contouring (p<0.001).

evidence.title: Collaborative strategies for deploying artificial intelligence to complement physician diagnoses of acute respiratory distress syndrome
evidence.outcome: Accuracy of physician-AI collaboration strategies versus physician alone and AI alone
evidence.effect: Collaboration strategies achieved 0.824-0.871 accuracy vs physician alone 0.808; physician-aided AI beat physician alone for 8/9 physicians, significantly for 3/9. Overreliance not assessed; physicians not shown AI output.
evidence.quote: For 8/9 physicians the physician-aided AI strategy outperformed the physician’s alone accuracy.

evidence.title: Optical Biopsy of Dysplasia in Barrett's Oesophagus Assisted by Artificial Intelligence
evidence.outcome: Gastroenterologist sensitivity and accuracy with versus without AI assistance at follow-up; overreliance assessed
evidence.effect: AI-assisted gastroenterologists had higher sensitivity (+20.0%, p=0.025) and accuracy (+12.22%, p=0.050) than unassisted ones at follow-up; untrained users showed reduced reliance on AI after training.
evidence.quote: When tested at 23.3 (±9.1) days after training, AI-assisted gastroenterologists maintained higher sensitivity (+20.0% (3.14–36.86), p = 0.025) and accuracy (+12.22% (0.03–24.48), p = 0.050) for recognizing dysplasia than the unassisted gastroenterologists.

evidence.title: Volume of hyperintense inflammation (VHI): A quantitative imaging biomarker of inflammation load in spondyloarthritis, enabled by human-machine cooperation
evidence.outcome: Inter-observer segmentation overlap (Dice) with versus without AI-assisted human-machine workflow
evidence.effect: Median Dice improved to 0.84 with the human-machine workflow versus 0.53–0.56 inter-reader for purely manual segmentation, an increase of 28–31%.
evidence.quote: Using the human-machine workflow, the median Dice scores improved to 0.84, representing an increase of 28–31% compared to pure manual segmentation.

evidence.title: BiTNet: Hybrid deep convolutional model for ultrasound image analysis of human biliary tract and its applications
evidence.outcome: Participant diagnostic accuracy and precision with versus without BiTNet assistance
evidence.effect: Mean accuracy and precision with BiTNet (0.74 and 0.61) were statistically higher than without (0.50 and 0.46), p<0.001; improved at all experience levels.
evidence.quote: The mean accuracy and precision of the participants with BiTNet as an assisting tool (0.74 and 0.61, respectively) are statistically higher than those of participants without the assisting tool (0.50 and 0.46, respectively (p<0.001)).

evidence.title: Quantitative assessment of myocardial fibrosis by digital image analysis: An adjunctive tool for pathologist "ground truth"
evidence.venue: Cardiovascular pathology : the official journal of the Society for Cardiovascular Pathology
evidence.outcome: Inter-observer agreement among pathologists before versus after seeing AI quantification of myocardial fibrosis
evidence.effect: Three pathologists reassessed fibrosis after seeing the algorithm output; overall agreement improved significantly and no longer depended on fibrosis severity. Algorithm median 13.60% vs first pathologist 8.33% (R2 0.79).
evidence.quote: The knowledge of the automatic quantification significantly improved the overall pathologist´s agreement, which became unaffected by the degree of MF severity.

evidence.title: Comprehensive clinical evaluation of deep learning-based auto-segmentation for radiotherapy in patients with cervical cancer
evidence.outcome: Contouring time and DSC for radiation oncologists with versus without AI auto-segmentation
evidence.effect: Median contouring time 82 min without vs 51 min with auto-segmentation; mean DSC 0.76 vs 0.82; HD 25.11 vs 24.40 mm; smaller SDs suggest reduced heterogeneity.
evidence.quote: The median times for contouring all OAR/CTVs without auto-segmentation and with auto-segmentation were 82 min (range, 66–101 min) and 51 min (range, 31–78 min), respectively.
evidence.sample_unit: abdominopelvic planning CT images (165 training, 15 validation)

evidence.title: Deep Neural Network Augments Performance of Junior Residents in Diagnosing COVID-19 Pneumonia on Chest Radiographs
evidence.outcome: Junior resident diagnostic performance with versus without AI assistance on external CXRs
evidence.effect: Residents' performance improved inversely to training level with AI assistance; two of three junior residents showed significant improvement.
evidence.quote: Among the three junior residents, two showed significant improvement with the assistance of AI.
evidence.sample_unit: external test chest radiographs read by 3 junior residents with and without AI

evidence.title: Clinical evaluation of a deep learning segmentation model including manual adjustments afterwards for locally advanced breast cancer
evidence.venue: Technical innovations & patient support in radiation oncology
evidence.outcome: AI-assisted versus manual contouring time
evidence.effect: Mean time reduction was 42.4% ± 26.5% for OARs and 58.5% ± 19.1% for CTVs.
evidence.quote: The time reduction (mean ± std) was 42.4% ± 26.5% and 58.5% ± 19.1% for OARs and CTVs, respectively, corresponding to an absolute mean reduction (hh:mm:ss) of 00:08:51 and 00:25:38.

evidence.title: Can incorrect artificial intelligence (AI) results impact radiologists, and if so, what can we do about it? A multi-reader pilot study of lung cancer detection with chest radiography
evidence.outcome: Reader performance with versus without AI, assessing overreliance on incorrect AI
evidence.effect: Compared with No AI, incorrect AI increased FN (2.7% to 20.7-33.0%) and FP (51.4% to 80.5-86.0%); correct AI improved accuracy.
evidence.quote: As anticipated, when AI provided correct positive and correct negative results, radiologists were more accurate in all AI conditions compared to the no AI condition.
evidence.sample_unit: radiologists (each reading 90 chest radiographs across 4 conditions)

evidence.title: Predicting DWI-FLAIR mismatch on NCCT: the role of artificial intelligence in hyperacute decision making
evidence.outcome: Inexperienced neurologists' DWI-FLAIR mismatch accuracy and AUC-ROC without vs with model output, lesions ≥15 mL
evidence.effect: In the subgroup with lesion volume ≥15 mL, accuracy improved from 0.537 to 0.610 and AUC-ROC from 0.493 to 0.613 with the model's results.
evidence.quote: In the subgroup with 15  mL or greater lesion volume, the evaluation of DWI-FLAIR mismatch from NCCT by inexperienced neurologists improved in accuracy (from 0.537 to 0.610) and AUC-ROC (from 0.493 to 0.613).

evidence.title: Enhanced artificial intelligence-based diagnosis using CBCT with internal denoising: Clinical validation for discrimination of fungal ball, sinusitis, and normal cases in the maxillary sinus
evidence.venue: Computer methods and programs in biomedicine
evidence.outcome: Human reader diagnostic accuracy with versus without AI assistance
evidence.effect: Human diagnosis accuracy improved by 11% (from 71.7 to 83.0%) with the proposed method; AI accuracy rose from 73.4 to 83.0% vs baseline. Overreliance not assessed.
evidence.quote: The external validation results for the unified diagnosis of sinus fungal ball, chronic rhinosinusitis, and normal cases show that the proposed method improves the micro-, macro-average area under the curve, and accuracy by 7.4, 5.6, and 9.6% (from 86.2, 87.0, and 73.4 to 93.6, 92.6, and 83.0%), respectively, compared with a baseline while improving human diagnosis accuracy by 11% (from 71.7 to 83.0%), demonstrating technical differentiation and clinical effectiveness.

evidence.title: A machine-learning approach to human ex vivo lung perfusion predicts transplantation outcomes and promotes organ utilization
evidence.outcome: EVLP specialist decisions with versus without model support in retrospective blinded implementation study
evidence.effect: InsighTx increased likelihood of transplanting suitable donor lungs (OR=13; 95% CI 4-45) and decreased likelihood of transplanting unsuitable lungs (OR=0.4; 95% CI 0.16-0.98).
evidence.quote: In a retrospective and blinded implementation study by EVLP specialists at our institution, InsighTx increased the likelihood of transplanting suitable donor lungs [odds ratio=13; 95% CI:4-45] and decreased the likelihood of transplanting unsuitable donor lungs [odds ratio=0.4; 95%CI:0.16-0.98].

evidence.title: Artificial intelligence suppression as a strategy to mitigate artificial intelligence automation bias
evidence.venue: Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association : JAMIA
evidence.outcome: Clinician diagnostic accuracy with versus without AI assistance; automation bias share of errors
evidence.effect: AI increased clinician accuracy from 87.2%±13.1% to 96.4%±1.9% (P<.001); automation bias accounted for 45.5% of errors in AI-assisted round.
evidence.quote: The AI significantly increased clinicians' accuracy from 87.2%±13.1% to 96.4%±1.9% (P < .001).
evidence.sample_unit: clinicians (each diagnosing 200 ACL MRIs with and without AI)

evidence.title: The auxiliary diagnosis of thyroid echogenic foci based on a deep learning segmentation model: A two-center study
evidence.outcome: Radiologist AUROC with versus without AI assistance across seniority levels
evidence.effect: Beginners' combined AUROC rose from 0.551 to 0.693; junior from 0.674 to 0.757; senior from 0.745 to 0.813 with AI-assisted strategies.
evidence.quote: The combined AUROC (0.693 [95% CI 0.595-0.791]) of radiology beginners using AI-assisted strategies was significantly higher than those without such strategies (0.551 [0.445-0.657]).

evidence.title: Development of an artificial intelligence bacteremia prediction model and evaluation of its impact on physician predictions focusing on uncertainty
evidence.outcome: Physician AUC for bacteremia prediction before vs after seeing AI output
evidence.effect: Post-AI physician AUC 0.703 (95% CI 0.654-0.753) vs pre-AI 0.639 (0.585-0.693); p<0.001, in sampled dataset N=1,000. Largest gains when physician uncertainty high and AI uncertainty low.
evidence.quote: The AUC of the post-AI physicians predictions (0.703, 95% CI 0.654-0.753) was significantly improved compared with that of the pre-AI predictions (0.639, 95% CI 0.585-0.693; p-value < 0.001) in the sampled dataset (N = 1,000).
evidence.sample_unit: ED patient cases sampled for physician pre-AI vs post-AI prediction

evidence.title: Web-Based Application Based on Human-in-the-Loop Deep Learning for Deidentifying Free-Text Data in Electronic Medical Records: Development and Usability Study
evidence.outcome: Human annotation time and accuracy with versus without AI preannotation
evidence.effect: For 200 notes annotated by one analyst, preannotation sped up annotation by 43% (95% CI 33.9-52.1; P <.001). Recall increased from 0.9756 to 0.9886 and micro-F1 from 0.9869 to 0.9922.
evidence.quote: Through the 5-round comparison, the preannotation by the trained model sped up the annotation work by 43% (95% CI 33.9-52.1; P <.001).

evidence.title: Pan-mediastinal neoplasm diagnosis via nationwide federated learning: a multicentre cohort study
evidence.outcome: Clinician top-1 and top-3 diagnostic accuracy with versus without CAIMEN-based software assistance
evidence.effect: 46 clinicians improved average top-1 accuracy by 19.1% and top-3 accuracy by 13.0% with AI assistance; CAIMEN alone also outperformed clinicians (top-1 0.500, top-3 0.800).
evidence.quote: with assistance from the computer aided diagnosis software based on CAIMEN, the 46 clinicians improved their average top-1 accuracy by 19·1% (0·345-0·411) and top-3 accuracy by 13·0% (0·545-0·616).
evidence.sample_unit: cases (development cohort: 7825 mediastinal neoplasm cases plus 796 normal controls)

evidence.title: Incorporation of CAD (computer-aided detection) with thin-slice lung CT in routine 18F-FDG PET/CT imaging read-out protocol for detection of lung nodules
evidence.outcome: Reader nodule detection, reading time and metastasis diagnosis with versus without CAD assistance
evidence.effect: CAD-assisted reading cut time about 33% versus diagnostic CT (60 s to 40 s). CAD found 49 extra nodules but missed 53. Nodule counts were similar (282 vs 283). Per-patient AUC did not differ significantly (0.799 vs 0.783).
evidence.quote: There was no superiority of the advanced dCT or CAD techniques regarding the diagnosis of metastasis.

evidence.title: Capsule endoscopy with artificial intelligence-assisted technology: Real-world usage of a validated AI model for capsule image review
evidence.outcome: Lesion capture and reading time with AI-assisted versus standard capsule reading by the same studies
evidence.effect: AI-assisted reading captured 98.1% of significant lesion images vs 86.2% for standard reading (P<0.001); mean reading time fell from 29.7 to 2.3 minutes; overall diagnosis agreed 100%.
evidence.quote: AI-assisted reading has shown significant time savings without reducing sensitivity in this study.

evidence.title: Comparison of clinical utility of deep learning-based systems for small-bowel capsule endoscopy reading
evidence.outcome: Endoscopist detection rate, reading time, and stress with versus without CNN screening
evidence.effect: Trainee detection rates did not differ significantly: A 77%, B 67%, C 79%. Reading time was 33.6 min without CNN vs 23.1 (existing) and 10.1 (novel). Stress was 3.2, 2.8, and 1.8.
evidence.quote: The detection rates of abnormalities by trainee endoscopists were not significantly different across the three processes: A, 77%; B, 67%; and C, 79%.

evidence.title: Augmented Decision-Making in wound Care: Evaluating the clinical utility of a Deep-Learning model for pressure injury staging
evidence.outcome: Pressure injury staging accuracy of participants without vs with CNN assistance
evidence.effect: Accuracy improved from 0.501 (95% CI 0.487-0.515) in Part I to 0.672 (95% CI 0.660-0.684) in Part II, a 17.1% improvement; Fleiss' kappa rose from 0.414 to 0.641.
evidence.quote: The accuracy of PI staging among participants was 0.501 (95% CI, 0.487-0.515) in Part I, improving by 17.1% to 0.672 (95% CI, 0.660-0.684) in Part II.
evidence.sample_unit: clinicians (dermatology residents, ward nurses, medical students)

evidence.title: Real-world validation of Artificial Intelligence-based Computed Tomography auto-contouring for prostate cancer radiotherapy planning
evidence.venue: Physics and imaging in radiation oncology
evidence.outcome: Inter-observer variability and contouring time with AI+editing vs manual contouring
evidence.effect: Inter-observer DSC improved with AI+edit (seminal vesicles 0.83 vs 0.73; prostate 0.88 vs 0.83; rectum 0.96 vs 0.81); editing time 3-7 min vs 17-24 min manual (p<0.01).
