evidence.quote: After automatic contouring and manual editing, inter-observer variability improved significantly, particularly for femoral heads + femurs, rectum and seminal vesicles.

evidence.title: Reader bias in breast cancer screening related to cancer prevalence and artificial intelligence decision support-a reader study
evidence.outcome: Reader sensitivity and specificity with vs without concurrent AI support; overreliance on erroneous AI
evidence.effect: Recall sensitivity fell from 81% (307/379) to 75% (284/379) with AI; specificity rose from 67% to 86%; net 23 fewer cancers detected; readers changed positive to negative in 21-41% of exams.
evidence.quote: When using AI, 39 of the cancers detected by study radiologists without AI were missed, and 16 cancers previously missed were detected with AI, resulting in a net decrease of 23 cancers detected when using AI decision support.

evidence.title: Detection of fibrosing interstitial lung disease-suspected chest radiographs using a deep learning-based computer-aided detection system: a retrospective, observational study
evidence.outcome: Reader sensitivity, specificity, accuracy and ROC-AUC without versus with AI assistance, non-experts and experts
evidence.effect: Non-expert ROC-AUC 0.795 to 0.825 (p=0.005); sensitivity 0.744 to 0.802 (p=0.003); no sensitivity change in experts (p=0.285); specificity and accuracy unchanged.
evidence.quote: After using BMAX, sensitivity was improved from 0.744 (95% CI; 0.697 to 0.791) to 0.802 (95% CI; 0.754 to 0.850) among non-experts (p=0.003), but not among experts (p=0.285).
evidence.sample_unit: chest radiograph images read by 25 physicians (20 non-experts, 5 experts)

evidence.title: Interpretable artificial intelligence-based app assists inexperienced radiologists in diagnosing biliary atresia from sonographic gallbladder images
evidence.outcome: Radiologist diagnostic AUC with versus without AI assistance in real-world mimic settings
evidence.effect: AI assistance raised average AUC from 0.773 to 0.835 for junior radiologists and from 0.749 to 0.805 for senior radiologists.
evidence.quote: Furthermore, the new model could aid both junior and senior radiologists to improve their diagnostic performances, with the average AUC increasing from 0.773 to 0.835 for junior radiologists and from 0.749 to 0.805 for senior radiologists.
evidence.sample_unit: prospectively collected sonographic gallbladder videos (from 207 infants) read by 18 radiologists

evidence.title: A Patient Similarity Network (CHDmap) to Predict Outcomes After Congenital Heart Surgery: Development and Validation Study
evidence.outcome: Clinician prediction of postoperative outcomes with versus without CHDmap support
evidence.effect: Clinicians substantially improved their predictive capabilities with CHDmap support; similar-patient poll beat the average of 3 clinicians; best AUROC 0.810 (complications) and 0.926 (ventilation duration).
evidence.quote: With the support of CHDmap, clinicians substantially improved their predictive capabilities.

evidence.title: Novel artificial intelligence-based hypodensity detection tool improves clinician identification of hypodensity on non-contrast computed tomography in stroke patients
evidence.outcome: Clinician hypodensity detection accuracy (DICE score) with versus without AI assistance
evidence.effect: Clinician mean DICE 0.33 before vs 0.40 after AI-based HDT; adjusted increase 0.07 (95% CI 0.02-0.11, p=0.003). Trainees improved by 0.09.
evidence.quote: AI-based HDT use was associated with an increase of 0.07 (95% CI: 0.02-0.11, p = 0.003) in DICE score accounting for individual scan and clinician effects.

evidence.title: Deep-learning for automated detection of MSU deposits on DECT: evaluating impact on efficiency and reader confidence
evidence.outcome: Reader time, diagnostic accuracy and confidence with versus without DL tool (paired reads, two readers)
evidence.effect: DL reduced reading time for trainee (p=0.02) but not attending (p=0.15); confidence unchanged (p=0.45); DL changed diagnosis in 3 cases, all correct with DL.
evidence.quote: The DL tool significantly reduced the reading time for the trainee radiologist (p = 0.02), but not for the attending radiologist (p = 0.15).
evidence.sample_unit: DECT studies (from different patients), each read with and without DL by 2 readers

evidence.title: Heterogeneity and predictors of the effects of AI assistance on radiologists
evidence.outcome: Radiologist performance with versus without AI assistance across 15 chest X-ray tasks; effect of AI errors
evidence.effect: AI assistance effects were heterogeneous across 140 radiologists; inaccurate AI predictions adversely affected radiologist performance on the aggregate of all pathologies and on half of the individual pathologies.
evidence.quote: Instead, we found that the occurrence of AI errors strongly influences treatment outcomes, with inaccurate AI predictions adversely affecting radiologist performance on the aggregate of all pathologies and on half of the individual pathologies investigated.

evidence.title: Artificial intelligence-assisted full-mouth radiograph mounting in dental education
evidence.outcome: Student mounting accuracy and speed with versus without AI pre-mounting
evidence.effect: AI-assisted group mounted faster (p < 0.05) but was less accurate than manual mounting (p < 0.01), showing that AI use can change user performance.
evidence.quote: Accuracy was lower in the test groups, when comparing AI-assisted and manual mounting of FMS (p < 0.01).

evidence.title: A Comparative Study of Large Language Models, Human Experts, and Expert-Edited Large Language Models to Neuro-Ophthalmology Questions
evidence.venue: Journal of neuro-ophthalmology : the official journal of the North American Neuro-Ophthalmology Society
evidence.outcome: quality and empathy with versus without AI
evidence.effect: Expert + AI beat Expert for quality (P < 0.0001) and empathy (P = 0.002); time was similar (P = 0.75).
evidence.quote: For quality ( P < 0.0001) and empathy ( P = 0.002), Expert + AI performed better than Expert.

evidence.title: The virtual reference radiologist: comprehensive AI assistance for clinical image reading and interpretation
evidence.outcome: Radiologist diagnostic accuracy and confidence with vs without GPT-4 assistance
evidence.effect: Top-3 diagnostic accuracy improved from 181/240 (75.4%) unassisted to 188/240 (78.3%) AI-assisted; diagnostic confidence significantly higher with AI assistance.
evidence.quote: When assessing if the correct diagnosis was among the top-3 differential diagnoses, diagnostic accuracy improved slightly from 181/240 (75.4%, unassisted) to 188/240 (78.3%, AI-assisted).
evidence.sample_unit: readings (6 radiologists x 40 imaging studies per session)

evidence.title: Deep learning-based platform performs high detection sensitivity of intracranial aneurysms in 3D brain TOF-MRA: An external clinical validation study
evidence.outcome: Radiologist sensitivity and accuracy with versus without AI assistance across experience levels
evidence.effect: With AI, mean SE rose (residents 71.40% vs 88.37%; attendings 82.79% vs 93.26%; professors 90.07% vs 97.44%; P<0.05) and ACC rose; SP unchanged. Overreliance not assessed.
evidence.quote: Utilizing the AI assistance, six radiologists (i.e., two residents, two attendings and two professors) achieved statistically significant improvements in mean SE (residents: 71.40 % vs. 88.37 %; attendings: 82.79 % vs. 93.26 %; professors: 90.07 % vs. 97.44 %; P < 0.05) and ACC (residents: 85.29 % vs. 94.12 %; attendings: 91.76 % vs. 97.06 %; professors: 95.29 % vs. 98.82 %; P < 0.05) while no statistically significant change was observed in SP.

evidence.title: Advancing Automatic Gastritis Diagnosis: An Interpretable Multilabel Deep Learning Framework for the Simultaneous Assessment of Multiple Indicators
evidence.outcome: Junior pathologists' false-negative rate and time per slide with versus without AI assistance
evidence.effect: False-negative rate 0.15 without vs 0.10 with model assistance; time per whole slide image reduced from 5.46 to 2.85 minutes.
evidence.quote: junior pathologists had lower false-negative rates with model assistance (0.15 versus 0.10).

evidence.title: Multi-Instance Learning for Vocal Fold Leukoplakia Diagnosis Using White Light and Narrow-Band Imaging: A Multicenter Study
evidence.outcome: Laryngologist AUC and accuracy with versus without AI assistance in human-machine comparison
evidence.effect: AI significantly improved AUC and accuracy for all 12 laryngologists (p < 0.05); diagnostic abilities and consistency improved, particularly for junior laryngologists.
evidence.quote: In the human-machine comparison, AI significantly improved AUC and accuracy for all laryngologists (p < 0.05).

evidence.title: Automatized self-supervised learning for skin lesion screening
evidence.outcome: Dermatologist confidence and agreement with top-10 AI-identified ugly ducklings when assisted by the tool
evidence.effect: Tool increased dermatologists' confidence in diagnosis; average majority agreement with top-10 AI-identified ugly ducklings reached 100% when assisted.
evidence.quote: The study also found that the tool increased dermatologists' confidence when formulating a diagnosis, and the average majority agreement with the top-10 AI-identified UDs reached 100% when assisted by our tool.

evidence.title: Deep learning for colorectal cancer detection in contrast-enhanced CT without bowel preparation: a retrospective, multicentre study
evidence.outcome: Radiologist detection accuracy with versus without DL assistance in intended use mode
evidence.effect: DL assistance improved radiologist accuracy: 93.4% vs 86.0% (internal test set) and 93.6% vs 85.3% (external test set 1), both p < 0.0001.
evidence.quote: In both the internal test set and external test set 1, the DL model yielded higher accuracy than that of radiologists (97.2% vs 86.0%, p < 0.0001; 94.9% vs 85.3%, p < 0.0001), and significantly improved the accuracy of radiologists (93.4% vs 86.0%, p < 0.0001; 93.6% vs 85.3%, p < 0.0001).
evidence.sample_unit: CT scans (cancer vs normal across internal, two external, and real-world test sets)

evidence.title: Use of an Artificial Intelligence-Generated Vascular Severity Score Improved Plus Disease Diagnosis in Retinopathy of Prematurity
evidence.outcome: Expert plus disease diagnosis agreement with reference standard, without vs with AI severity score assistance
evidence.effect: Weighted κ improved from 0.69 to 0.81; AUC from 0.94 to 0.98 (difference 0.04); AUPR from 0.86 to 0.95 (difference 0.09).
evidence.quote: Expert agreement improved significantly, from substantial (κ value, 0.69 [0.59, 0.75]) to near perfect (κ value, 0.81 [0.71, 0.86]), when AI-based VSS was integrated.

evidence.title: Improving Clinician Performance in Classifying EEG Patterns on the Ictal-Interictal Injury Continuum Using Interpretable Machine Learning
evidence.outcome: Clinician EEG pattern classification accuracy with versus without AI assistance
evidence.effect: Mean user diagnostic accuracy improved from 47 to 71% (P<0.04) with AI assistance among eight medical professionals.
evidence.quote: Mean user diagnostic accuracy improved from 47 to 71% (P<0.04).
evidence.sample_unit: clinicians (medical professionals classifying 100 EEG samples with and without AI)

evidence.title: Artificial Intelligence Efficacy as a Function of Trainee Interpreter Proficiency: Lessons from a Randomized Controlled Trial
evidence.outcome: Reader accuracy with versus without AI aid, and reliance on incorrect AI results, by trainee level
evidence.effect: Medical student accuracy improved 11.0 points (P<.001) with aid; residents no significant change. Both groups considerably less accurate when disagreeing with or given incorrect AI results; students less accurate than AI alone.
evidence.quote: Both groups were considerably less accurate when disagreeing with the artificial intelligence or when supplied with an incorrect artificial intelligence result.

evidence.title: The clinical value of artificial intelligence in assisting junior radiologists in thyroid ultrasound: a multicenter prospective study from real clinical practice
evidence.outcome: Junior and senior radiologist diagnostic performance with versus without AI assistance
evidence.effect: Junior+AI improved specificity 0.837 to 0.921, accuracy 0.833 to 0.895, AUC 0.829 to 0.871 (all p<0.001), with no sensitivity gain; the AI alone had AUC 0.901, and the senior+AI gain was not significant.
evidence.quote: Compared to independent readings by junior radiologists, AI-assisted readings significantly improved their specificity, accuracy, and AUC (0.837 vs. 0.921, 0.833 vs. 0.895, 0.829 vs. 0.871, respectively; all p < 0.001), where specificity and accuracy were comparable to those of senior radiologists ( p > 0.05) (Table 4 ).

evidence.title: Cutting Edge to Cutting Time: Can ChatGPT Improve the Radiologist's Reporting?
evidence.venue: Journal of imaging informatics in medicine
evidence.outcome: Reporting time and report quality with versus without GPT-4 assistance
evidence.effect: Total and case reporting times decreased with AI assistance but not significantly (p>0.05); quality of finalized reports comparable with no significant differences. Time excluding editing was significantly lower (p<0.05).
evidence.quote: Quality scores of the finalized reports with and without AI-assistance were comparable with no significant differences.

evidence.title: Assessing breast disease with deep learning model using bimodal bi-view ultrasound images and clinical information
evidence.outcome: Radiologist diagnostic AUC with versus without AI aid
evidence.effect: BreNet-aided scheme increased the pooled AUC of the radiologists from 0.841 to 0.934 for reviewing images, and from 0.892 to 0.934 in the real-world test.
evidence.quote: BreNet-aided scheme increased the pooled AUC of the radiologists from 0.841 to 0.934 for reviewing images, and from 0.892 to 0.934 in the real-world test.

evidence.title: Comparison of the Quality of Discharge Letters Written by Large Language Models and Junior Clinicians: Single-Blinded Study
evidence.outcome: GPT-4 vs junior clinician discharge letter quality rated by blinded primary care physicians
evidence.effect: GPT-4 higher on information provision (4.32 vs 3.70, P=.03); no significant differences in clarity, collegiality, conciseness, follow-up, or overall satisfaction (3.96 vs 3.62, P=.36).
evidence.quote: GPT-4 outperformed human counterparts in information provision (mean 4.32, SD 0.95 vs 3.70, SD 1.27; P=.03) and had no instances of hallucination.
evidence.sample_unit: letter ratings (5 cases rated by primary care physicians, GPT-4 vs junior clinician letters)

evidence.title: Potential of E-Learning Interventions and Artificial Intelligence-Assisted Contouring Skills in Radiotherapy: The ELAISA Study
evidence.outcome: Contour quality (DSC) and time for radiation oncologists with vs without AI-assisted contouring
evidence.effect: AI assistance raised DSC for optic nerve (0.05), oral cavity (0.10), parotid (0.07), spinal cord (0.04), mandible (0.02) and cut contouring time (e.g., mandible -6.60 min); 24% of AI contours accepted unedited.
evidence.quote: Regardless of teaching, AI-assisted contouring increased contouring quality and reduced contouring time for most investigated OARs.
evidence.country: Multiple low- and middle-income countries (23 institutions, IAEA); cases from Denmark

evidence.title: The potential benefit of artificial intelligence regarding clinical decision-making in the treatment of wrist trauma patients
evidence.venue: Journal of orthopaedic surgery and research
evidence.outcome: Physician diagnostic performance with versus without AI assistance on wrist trauma cases
evidence.effect: AI-supported group diagnosed without additional CT or senior consultation in 75% vs 52% of cases (p = 0.003); fewer added CTs (14% vs 28%, p = 0.02); sensitivity 1.00 vs 0.96 (p = 0.06).
evidence.quote: The AI-supported group was able to make a diagnosis without support (no additional CT, no senior consultation) in significantly more of the cases than the control group (75% vs. 52%, p = 0.003).

evidence.title: Real-world application of a 3D deep learning model for detecting and localizing cerebral microbleeds
evidence.outcome: Reader sensitivity per lesion and false positives per patient with versus without AI assistance
evidence.effect: Sensitivity with AI vs without: reader 1 0.991 vs 0.905 (p=0.132), reader 2 0.922 vs 0.621 (p=0.017), reader 3 0.966 vs 0.871 (p=0.227). FPs per patient did not differ significantly.
evidence.quote: In particular, radiology residents (reader 2) showed a statistically significant increase in sensitivity per lesion when using AI.

evidence.title: Impact of a deep learning-based brain CT interpretation algorithm on clinical decision-making for intracranial hemorrhage in the emergency department
evidence.outcome: Clinician diagnostic performance and decision consistency for intracranial hemorrhage without versus with AI, by experience level
evidence.effect: Experienced participants were minimally affected. Inexperienced participants' sensitivity rose 59.33% to 72.67% and specificity fell 65.49% to 53.73% (both p<0.001), with decision changes driven mainly by AI false positives.
evidence.quote: In contrast, inexperienced participants exhibited significantly increased sensitivity (59.33-72.67%, p < 0.001) and decreased specificity (65.49-53.73%, p < 0.001) with the algorithm.

evidence.title: Grading of diabetic retinopathy using a pre-segmenting deep learning classification model: Validation of an automated algorithm
evidence.outcome: Grader agreement with gold standard with vs without AI assistance (weighted kappa, sensitivity)
evidence.effect: Weighted kappa 0.88 (grader alone) vs 0.89 (grader with DL assistance); sensitivity 95% vs 94%; specificity 82% vs 84%. Almost identical performance; assistance identified 5 additional level 1 images.
evidence.quote: Models 1 and 2 achieved an almost identical performance in the grading DR on retinal images across all levels of DR, with a weighted kappa of 0.88 and 0.89, respectively.

evidence.title: Large Language Model Influence on Diagnostic Reasoning: A Randomized Clinical Trial
evidence.outcome: Physician diagnostic reasoning score with versus without LLM access, compared with LLM alone
evidence.effect: Median score 76% (LLM group) vs 74% (conventional), adjusted difference 2 percentage points (95% CI -4 to 8; P=.60); LLM alone scored 16 points higher than conventional group (P=.03).
evidence.quote: The LLM alone demonstrated higher performance than both physician groups, indicating the need for technology and workforce development to realize the potential of physician-artificial intelligence collaboration in clinical practice.

evidence.title: OSAIRIS: Lessons Learned From the Hospital-Based Implementation and Evaluation of an Open-Source Deep-Learning Model for Radiotherapy Image Segmentation
evidence.venue: Clinical oncology (Royal College of Radiologists (Great Britain))
evidence.outcome: AI-assisted contouring time
evidence.effect: Time-saving was 36% (5.4 ± 2.1 minutes) for prostate and 67% (30.3 ± 8.7 minutes) for head and neck contouring.
evidence.quote: We found that OSAIRIS affords a significant time-saving of 36% (5.4 ± 2.1 minutes) when used for prostate contouring and 67% (30.3 ± 8.7 minutes) for head and neck contouring.

evidence.title: Deep Learning Algorithms for Breast Cancer Detection in a UK Screening Cohort: As Stand-alone Readers and Combined with Human Readers
evidence.outcome: human-AI reading versus double reading
evidence.effect: DL+human sensitivity 67.0%, 65.6%, 65.4% vs double reading 67.4%; specificity 97.4%, 97.6%, 97.6% vs 97.1%; P<.001 for all.
evidence.quote: Combining the DL algorithms with human readers achieved noninferior sensitivity (67.0%, 65.6%, and 65.4% for DL-1, DL-2, and DL-3, respectively; P < .001 for all) compared with double reading (67.4%), and superior specificity (97.4%, 97.6%, and 97.6%; P < .001 for all) compared with double reading (97.1%).

evidence.title: Artificial intelligence-assisted delineation for postoperative radiotherapy in patients with lung cancer: a prospective, multi-center, cohort study
evidence.outcome: Contouring accuracy and time for residents with AI assistance versus fully manual delineation
evidence.effect: AI-assisted CTV median DSC 0.745 vs 0.703, HD 20.03 vs 21.55 mm, MDA 2.57 vs 3.06 mm (all P<0.05); CTV time cut ~43.2%, OAR time ~56.2%.
evidence.quote: AI-assisted CTV and OARs delineation for PORT significantly improves the accuracy and efficiency in the real-world setting, compared with pure AI auto-segmentation or fully manual delineation by junior oncologists.

evidence.title: The Future of Surgical Diagnostics: Artificial Intelligence-Enhanced Detection of Ganglion Cells for Hirschsprung Disease
evidence.venue: Laboratory investigation; a journal of technical methods and pathology
evidence.outcome: Pathologist diagnostic accuracy and time with versus without AI heatmap support
evidence.effect: Accuracy rose from 77% to 85.8% with model heatmap support; diagnosis time fell from 139.7 to 70.5 seconds. Overreliance was not assessed.
evidence.quote: In the reader study, on average, the pathologists' diagnostic accuracy increased from 77% to 85.8% with the model's heatmap support, whereas the diagnosis time decreased from an average of 139.7 to 70.5 seconds.
evidence.sample_unit: patients (668 slides; 10 pathologists read 50 frozen WSIs in reader study)

evidence.title: A randomized controlled trial on evaluating clinician-supervised generative AI for decision support
evidence.outcome: Performance of users with different AI configurations (autonomous vs clinician-supervised) compared to non-AI paper guide
evidence.effect: Supervised-ChatGPT had significantly higher decision accuracy than paper guide and autonomous ChatGPT; lower LF/HF ratio; highest trust; longer completion time.
evidence.quote: Results indicate that the Supervised-ChatGPT group showed significantly higher decision accuracy compared to the paper guide and ChatGPT groups, although the scenario completion time was longer.

evidence.title: Development and validation of a deep learning pipeline to diagnose ovarian masses using ultrasound screening: a retrospective multicenter study
evidence.outcome: Reader accuracy, sensitivity and specificity with versus without AI assistance for ovarian mass diagnosis
evidence.effect: Junior/intermediate radiologists improved with AI (ACC 80.8 vs 75.3, p=0.00015; SEN 79.5 vs 74.6, p=0.029; SPE 81.7 vs 75.8, p=0.0032); GPs with AI reached radiologist-level performance.
evidence.quote: There was a significant improvement in junior and intermediate radiologists who were assisted by AI compared to those who were not assisted by AI (ACC: 80.8 vs. 75.3, p = 0.00015; SEN: 79.5 vs. 74.6, p = 0.029; SPE: 81.7 vs. 75.8, p = 0.0032).

evidence.title: EyeGPT for Patient Inquiries and Medical Education: Development and Validation of an Ophthalmology Large Language Model
evidence.outcome: Ophthalmologist answers ranked best with vs without EyeGPT assistance
evidence.effect: EyeGPT-assisted ophthalmologists ranked best in accuracy for 94 (78.3%) and trustworthiness for 93 (77.5%) of 120 questions; unassisted ophthalmologists ranked best for 14 (11.7%) and 15 (12.5%).
evidence.quote: With the assistance of EyeGPT, the answers provided by the ophthalmologists excelled, ranking highest in accuracy and trustworthiness in 94 (78.3%) and 93 (77.5%) of the 120 questions, respectively.

evidence.title: Optimising the paradigms of human AI collaborative clinical coding
evidence.outcome: Coder performance with vs without AI assistance, and compared with AI alone, by experience level
evidence.effect: Senior and junior coders with AI outperformed both human-only and AI-only setups; interns with AI still fell short of AI alone. HITL mode outperformed simplified ACC mode and manual coding.
evidence.quote: In contrast, the senior and junior clinical coders outperform both the human-only and AI-only setups, which demonstrates the positive impact of collaborative coding approach.

evidence.title: Artificial intelligence improves bronchoscopy performance: a randomised crossover trial
evidence.outcome: Bronchoscopist performance with versus without AI guidance on a phantom: segments inspected, structured progressions, time
evidence.effect: With AI guidance: +6.0 segments inspected (p<0.001), +5.2 structured progressions (p<0.001), +72 s procedure time (p<0.001); significant in novices, intermediates and experienced.
evidence.quote: AI guidance caused the participants to inspect more segments (mean difference, paired t-test: +6.0 segments, p<0.001), perform more structured progressions (+5.2 progressions, p<0.001) and spend more time on the procedure (+72 s, p<0.001) compared to their standard procedures.
evidence.country: International (six continents; ERS conference, Milan, Italy)

evidence.title: AI-assisted radiologists vs. standard double reading for rib fracture detection on CT images: A real-world clinical study
evidence.outcome: Sensitivity at patient level
evidence.effect: AI-assisted radiologists improved sensitivity to 94.2%, compared to 69.2% for standard double-reading.
evidence.quote: The sensitivity at patient level was estimated at 94.2% in AI-assisted group and 69.2% in double-reading, with an increase estimated at 25.0% (95% CI: 10.5, 39.5; P < 0.001).

evidence.title: A deep learning model for carotid plaques detection based on CTA images: a two stepwise early-stage clinical validation study
evidence.outcome: Radiologist plaque-detection sensitivity with versus without AI assistance in simulated clinical scenarios
evidence.effect: The model improved radiologists' sensitivity in diagnosing plaques in the Model-human study. Overreliance was not reported as assessed, and no numbers are given in the abstract.
evidence.quote: Furthermore, in Model-human Real Clinical Scenarios study, we found that the model improved the radiologists' sensitivity in diagnosing plaques.

evidence.title: GPT-4 assistance for improvement of physician performance on patient care tasks: a randomized controlled trial
evidence.outcome: Physician management reasoning score with GPT-4 plus conventional resources versus conventional resources alone
evidence.effect: LLM-assisted physicians scored 6.5% higher (95% CI 2.7 to 10.2, P<0.001); no significant difference between LLM-augmented physicians and LLM alone (-0.9%, P=0.8); LLM users spent 119.3 s more per case.
evidence.quote: Physicians using the LLM scored significantly higher compared to those using conventional resources (mean difference = 6.5%, 95% confidence interval (CI) = 2.7 to 10.2, P < 0.001).

evidence.title: Safety of human-AI cooperative decision-making within intensive care: A physical simulation study
evidence.outcome: Human-AI team behavior in a high-fidelity simulation, including AI influence on physician decisions
evidence.effect: Physicians changed prescriptions in 46% (105/228) of trials after seeing AI advice; unsafe recommendations mostly rejected, showing human-AI behavior needs assessment beyond standalone AI.
evidence.quote: Physicians changed their prescription (dose of fluids and/or vasopressors) in 46 ± 3% (105/228), 95% CI: 0.40–0.52, of trials after seeing what the AI suggested.

evidence.title: Improving the Real-Time Classification of Disease Severity in Ulcerative Colitis: Artificial Intelligence as the Trigger for a Second Opinion
evidence.outcome: Non-IBD expert performance with versus without AI support
evidence.effect: When used as a supporting system, the AI improved non-IBD experts' performance by 12% and disagreed with the primary physician in 20%-39% of cases.
evidence.quote: When used as a supporting system, it improved non-IBD experts' performance by 12% and disagreed with the primary physician in 20%-39% of cases.

evidence.title: Physician clinical decision modification and bias assessment in a randomized controlled trial of AI assistance
evidence.outcome: Physician decision accuracy with versus without GPT-4 assistance (pre-post) in chest pain vignettes
evidence.effect: Accuracy improved from 47% to 65% (white male patient) and 63% to 80% (Black female patient); improvement about 18% in both groups.
evidence.quote: The accuracy improvement occurs without introducing or exacerbating demographic biases, with both groups showing similar magnitudes of improvement (18%).

evidence.title: Evaluation of a novel ensemble model for preoperative ovarian cancer diagnosis: Clinical factors, O-RADS, and deep learning radiomics
evidence.outcome: Sonographer diagnostic AUC with versus without ensemble model assistance
evidence.effect: Sonographers' average AUC improved by 11% in the internal validation set and by 7.7% in the external validation set with the ensemble model.
evidence.quote: The sonographers' average AUC improved by 11 % in the internal validation set and by 7.7 % in the external validation set.

evidence.title: Human-AI collaboration in large language model-assisted brain MRI differential diagnosis: a usability study
evidence.outcome: Reader differential diagnosis accuracy with LLM assistance versus conventional internet search
evidence.effect: 70/114 (61.4%) correct with LLM assistance vs 53/114 (46.5%) conventional, p = 0.033; no difference in interpretation time or confidence.
evidence.quote: LLM-assisted brain MRI differential diagnosis yielded superior accuracy (70/114; 61.4% (LLM-assisted) vs 53/114; 46.5% (conventional) correct diagnoses, p = 0.033, chi-square test).
evidence.sample_unit: radiology residents (240 case readings across 40 brain MRI cases)

evidence.title: Psychological Factors Influencing Appropriate Reliance on AI-enabled Clinical Decision Support Systems: Experimental Web-Based Study Among Dermatologists
evidence.outcome: Dermatologist accuracy with versus without AI support in lesion classification
evidence.effect: Accuracy improved significantly with AI support (t222=-3.3; P<.001) but only by an average of 1%.
evidence.quote: A 2-tailed t test revealed that participants' accuracy improved significantly with AI support (t<sub>222</sub>=-3.3; P<.001; Cohen d=4.5), but only by an average of 1% (1/100).

evidence.title: Labor-Efficient Pathological Auxiliary Diagnostic Model for Primary and Metastatic Tumor Tissue Detection in Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma
evidence.venue: Modern pathology : an official journal of the United States and Canadian Academy of Pathology, Inc
evidence.outcome: Pathologist diagnostic accuracy and time with vs without AI assistance for lymph node metastasis detection
evidence.effect: PANseg augmented the diagnostic accuracy of 6 pathologists from 0.888 to 0.961, while reducing the average diagnostic time by 32.6% (72.0 vs 48.5 minutes).
evidence.quote: In lymph node metastasis detection, PANseg augmented the diagnostic accuracy of 6 pathologists from 0.888 to 0.961, while reducing the average diagnostic time by 32.6% (72.0 vs 48.5 minutes).

evidence.title: The Real-World Impact of Vestibular Schwannoma Fully Automated Volume Measures on the Evaluation of Size Change and Clinical Management Outcomes in a Multidisciplinary Meeting Setting
evidence.venue: The journal of international advanced otology
evidence.outcome: Effect of AI volume measures on radiological classification and management decisions in simulated MDMs
evidence.effect: AI volumes changed radiological classification of size change (z=2.49, P=.01) but not management decisions (z=0.30, P=.76) versus linear measures.
evidence.quote: Provision of fully automated VS volume measurements to "real-world" MDM preparation significantly impacted the radiological classification of VS size change but did not influence management decisions.

evidence.title: Clinician-artificial intelligence collaboration: A win-win solution for efficiency and reliability in atrial fibrillation diagnosis
evidence.outcome: PAF detection accuracy and clinician workload with clinician-AI collaboration versus clinician alone or AI alone
evidence.effect: Clinicians alone missed 13.7% of PAF patients; AI alone misidentified 23.3% of non-AF patients as PAF. Collaboration correctly identified all patients and reduced clinician workload by 76.7%.
evidence.quote: After implementing the proposed clinician-AI collaboration strategy, all patients were correctly identified, and clinicians' workload was reduced by 76.7%.

evidence.title: Artificial Intelligence for Low-Dose CT Lung Cancer Screening: Comparison of Utilization Scenarios
evidence.outcome: Recall rate, specificity, sensitivity and time for radiologists with vs without AI assistance
evidence.effect: AI assistant: recall 30.3% vs 22.1% (p<.001), specificity 81.1% vs 88.8%, sensitivity 64.8% vs 64.2% (p=.86), time 161 vs 164 s (p=.48).
evidence.quote: Compared with interpretation without AI (recall rate, 22.1%; per-nodule sensitivity, 64.2%; per-examination specificity, 88.8%; mean interpretation time, 164 seconds), AI as an assistant showed higher recall rate (30.3%; p < .001), lower per-examination specificity (81.1%), and no significant change in per-nodule sensitivity (64.8%; p = .86) or mean interpretation time (161 seconds; p = .48)

evidence.title: AI for fracture diagnosis in clinical practice: Four approaches to systematic AI-implementation and their impact on AI-effectiveness
evidence.outcome: False negatives and false positives of radiologist alone versus radiologist plus AI under four implementation modes
evidence.effect: Radiologist 2.7% FN (40/1508); AI-safety net 0.07% FN (1/1508), FP 7.6%; AI-problem-solving 3.2% FN; AI-triage 2.1% FN; all changes p<0.001.
evidence.quote: Implementation methods have a large impact on AI-effectiveness.

evidence.title: Nephrologist's Perceptions of Risk of Severe Chronic Kidney Disease and Outpatient Follow-up After Hospitalization With AKI: Multinational Randomized Survey Study
evidence.venue: Canadian journal of kidney health and disease
evidence.outcome: Clinician follow-up decisions with versus without AI risk prediction in randomized vignettes
evidence.effect: Randomized comparison showed risk reporting changed decisions: <10% risk mean difference -0.71; ≥50% risk mean difference 0.49; OR 0.35 and 2.21 for score ≥5.
evidence.quote: When the predicted risk of severe CKD is reported, nephrologists are less likely to recommend follow-up for lower risk patients with AKI and more likely to recommend follow-up for higher risk patients, leading to better alignment of recommendations for outpatient follow-up with patient risk of severe CKD.

evidence.title: Predicting onward care needs at admission to reduce discharge delay using explainable machine learning
evidence.outcome: Accuracy of combined clinician-plus-machine predictions versus either alone
evidence.effect: Hybrid clinician-ML model achieved OVR AUROC 0.936 [0.928 0.943], more accurate than ML alone (0.915).
evidence.quote: Finally, we demonstrate that combining clinician and machine predictions, in a hybrid model, provides even more accurate early predictions of onward social care requirements (OVR AUROC = 0.936 [0.928 0.943]) and demonstrates the potential for human-in-the-loop decision support systems in clinical practice.

evidence.title: The impact of AI feedback on the accuracy of diagnosis, decision switching and trust in radiography
evidence.outcome: Radiographer diagnostic accuracy with vs without AI feedback (heatmap, binary), including overreliance when AI incorrect
evidence.effect: AI feedback improved accuracy overall (AI correct +13.4 points) but reduced it when AI incorrect (-4.8 overall; -9.6 students); heatmap lowered accuracy in pathological cases (65.85% to 57.62%) before binary feedback raised it (72.35%).
evidence.quote: The AI feedback (i.e., heatmap and binary AI decision) proved beneficial to participants except for situations where the AI was incorrect and pathological examinations in the student group (decrease in accuracy of 3.4%).

evidence.title: Large Language Models for Diagnosing Focal Liver Lesions From CT/MRI Reports: A Comparative Study With Radiologists
evidence.venue: Liver international : official journal of the International Association for the Study of the Liver
evidence.outcome: Radiologist diagnostic accuracy with versus without LLM assistance
evidence.effect: No incremental diagnostic value of ChatGPT-4o for any radiologist (p-values 0.63 to >0.99), although standalone LLM accuracy matched junior radiologists.
evidence.quote: No incremental diagnostic value of ChatGPT-4o was observed for any radiologist (p-values, 0.63 to > 0.99).

evidence.title: Augmented reality microscopy to bridge trust between AI and pathologists
evidence.outcome: Pathologist interobserver agreement at PD-L1 CPS ≥5 with vs without AI assistance
evidence.effect: Fleiss' kappa rose from 0.52 (manual) to 0.76 (AI-assisted), p<0.01; agreement among all 11 pathologists 43% vs 69%; any two 77% vs 91%.
evidence.quote: Agreement among pathologists by Fleiss’ Kappa showed overall improved agreement from 0.52 (0.40–0.65) with manual scoring on day 1 to 0.76 (0.62-0.87) with AI-assisted scoring on day 2 with statistical significance ( p < 0.01, Bootstrapping of differences) (Fig. 3 c).
evidence.sample_unit: pathologists scoring 35 biopsy regions of interest

evidence.title: Artificial intelligence algorithm improves radiologists' bone age assessment accuracy
evidence.venue: Journal of the Chinese Medical Association : JCMA
evidence.outcome: Radiologist bone age accuracy (MAD) with vs without AI assistance, and automation bias assessed
evidence.effect: MAD improved from 0.74 to 0.46 years with AI (p<0.001); >1 year error proportion 24.0% vs 8.4%; improved predictions 16.8% vs worsened 2.3%; less experienced radiologists prone to automation bias.
evidence.quote: The overall accuracy of senior, mid-level, and junior radiologists improved significantly with AI assistance than without AI assistance (MAD: 0.74 vs 0.46 years, p < 0.001; proportion of assessments for which MAD exceeded 1 year: 24.0% vs 8.4%, p < 0.001).

evidence.title: Enhancing the Accuracy of Human Phenotype Ontology Identification: Comparative Evaluation of Multimodal Large Language Models
evidence.outcome: HPO description accuracy of physicians with vs without MLLM assistance, plus standalone MLLM accuracy
evidence.quote: Of the 270 descriptions collected from each group, the MLLM-assisted group achieved a correctness rate of 67.4% (182/270), while the manual group achieved 20.4% (55/270).
evidence.sample_unit: junior physicians (27 patient images each, 540 descriptions)

evidence.title: A multimodal vision foundation model for clinical dermatology
evidence.outcome: Clinician diagnostic accuracy with versus without AI assistance in reader studies
evidence.effect: AI assistance improved clinicians' skin cancer diagnostic accuracy by 11% on dermoscopy images and nondermatologist providers' differential diagnosis by 16.5% across 128 conditions.
evidence.quote: PanDerm outperformed clinicians by 10.2% in early-stage melanoma detection through longitudinal analysis, improved clinicians' skin cancer diagnostic accuracy by 11% on dermoscopy images and enhanced nondermatologist healthcare providers' differential diagnosis by 16.5% across 128 skin conditions on clinical photographs.
evidence.country: multiple (11 clinical institutions, not specified in text)

evidence.title: Improved diagnostic decision making for microvascular invasion in HCC using a novel nomogram incorporating delta radiomics and body composition factors: A multicenter study
evidence.venue: European journal of surgical oncology : the journal of the European Society of Surgical Oncology and the British Association of Surgical Oncology
evidence.outcome: Radiologist diagnostic accuracy for MVI with versus without nomogram assistance
evidence.effect: Nomogram assistance improved radiologists' diagnostic accuracy for MVI by up to 13.4 percentage points.
evidence.quote: The nomogram's implementation enhanced radiologists' diagnostic accuracy for MVI by up to 13.4 percentage points.

evidence.title: Human-AI collectives most accurately diagnose clinical vignettes
evidence.venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
evidence.outcome: Diagnostic accuracy of physicians alone, LLMs alone, and hybrid human-LLM collectives (top-k, MRR)
evidence.effect: Hybrid collectives outperformed single physicians, physician collectives, single LLMs and LLM ensembles; adding one LLM to physicians consistently increased performance; adding a physician raised all LLMs' accuracy. Simulated aggregation, not real users.
evidence.quote: Crucially, adding one LLM to the human diagnoses consistently increased performance for both individual physicians and human-only ensembles of different sizes, with the largest increase attained when adding the best-performing individual LLM or an all-LLM ensemble.
evidence.sample_unit: text-based medical case vignettes (40,762 physician differential diagnoses)

evidence.title: Whole-lesion-aware network based on freehand ultrasound video for breast cancer assessment: a prospective multicenter study
evidence.venue: Cancer imaging : the official publication of the International Cancer Imaging Society
evidence.outcome: Radiologist performance with versus without AI assistance in reader study
evidence.effect: With WAUVE assistance, average specificity of four radiologists improved by 6.67% and consistency rose from 0.807 to 0.838.
evidence.quote: With the WAUVE model assistance, the average specificity of four experienced radiologists was improved by 6.67%, and higher consistency was achieved (from 0.807 to 0.838).

evidence.title: Empirically derived evaluation requirements for responsible deployments of AI in safety-critical settings
evidence.outcome: Nurse performance with vs without AI recommendations, by AI correctness, assessing overreliance in joint human-AI system
evidence.effect: With AI recommendations nurses improved when AI was most correct (+52.8% emergency, +67.4% non-emergency) but worsened when AI was most misleading (−120.5% emergency, −96.3% non-emergency) versus no AI.
evidence.quote: Compared to nurses working without AI augmentation, nurses working with AI recommendations performed better on both emergency ( + 52.8%, odds ratio = 1.86, 95% CI [1.49, 2.23], z = 6.06, p < 0.001) and non-emergency ( + 67.4%, odds ratio = 1.62, 95% CI [1.35, 1.89], z = 5.59, p < 0.001) cases when the AI algorithm was most correct, but worse on both emergency (−120.5%, odds ratio = 0.414, 95% CI [0.327, 0.501], z = −8.25, p < 0.001) and non-emergency (−96.3%, odds ratio = 0.418, 95% CI [0.333, 0.503], z = −8.41, p < 0.001) cases when the AI algorithm was most erroneous or misleading.
evidence.sample_unit: participants (450 nursing students and 12 licensed nurses; 4125 case records analyzed)

evidence.title: Artificial intelligence-assisted detection of nasopharyngeal carcinoma on endoscopic images: a national, multicentre, model development and validation study
evidence.outcome: Otolaryngologist diagnostic accuracy with versus without AI assistance in multireader multicase study
evidence.effect: Primary care otolaryngologists' accuracy rose 7.9%, from 83.4% (95% CI 80.1-86.7) without AI to 91.2% (88.6-93.9) with AI (p<0.0001); reading time fell from 6.7 s to 5.0 s.
evidence.quote: In the multireader, multicase study, the artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted strategy enhanced otolaryngologists' diagnostic accuracy by 7·9%, increasing from 83·4% (95% CI 80·1-86·7, without AI assistance) to 91·2% (95% CI 88·6-93·9, with AI assistance; p<0·0001) for primary care otolaryngologists.
evidence.sample_unit: images read in multireader multicase study by 28 otolaryngologists

evidence.title: Multimodal Generative Artificial Intelligence Model for Creating Radiology Reports for Chest Radiographs in Patients Undergoing Tuberculosis Screening
evidence.outcome: reader detection accuracy with versus without AI
evidence.effect: Detection accuracy was significantly higher with AI for one reader (reader 1: p = .47; reader 2: p = .03).
evidence.quote: Accuracy was significantly lower for AI-generated reports than for both readers alone (p < .001), but significantly higher with than without AI-generated reports for one reader (reader 1: p = .47; reader 2: p = .03).
evidence.country: Unknown (public datasets from tuberculosis screening programs)

evidence.title: External validation of an artificial intelligence tool for fracture detection in children with osteogenesis imperfecta: a multireader study
evidence.outcome: Radiologist per-examination accuracy without versus with AI assistance
evidence.effect: Radiologist accuracy rose from 83.4% [95% CI 75.2, 89.8] unaided to 90.7% [83.5, 95.4] with AI, despite AI alone at 74.8%.
evidence.quote: Radiologists using AI assistance improved average radiologist accuracy per examination to 90.7% [95% CI: 83.5%, 95.4%].

evidence.title: Real-Life Performance of a Commercially Available AI Tool for Post-Traumatic Intracranial Hemorrhage Detection on CT Scans: A Supportive Tool
evidence.outcome: Sensitivity and accuracy of junior residents alone, AI alone, and residents with AI assistance for ICH detection
evidence.effect: AI sensitivity 88.8%, junior residents 85.7%; with AI assistance combined sensitivity 95.2% and overall accuracy 98.8%. AI detected two of three ICH cases missed by residents.
evidence.quote: When AI assistance was integrated, the combined sensitivity improved to 95.2%, and the overall accuracy reached 98.8%.

evidence.title: Deep Learning-Enabled Ultrasound for Advancing Anterior Talofibular Ligament Injuries Classification: A Multicenter Model Development and Validation Study
evidence.outcome: Radiologist accuracy with versus without AI aid when reviewing ultrasound images
evidence.effect: ATFLNet-aided strategy improved radiologists' average accuracy from 0.707 to 0.811 (p<.001); in simulated scenario 0.794 to 0.864 (p=.003), with reduced variability especially for juniors.
evidence.quote: ATFLNet-aided strategy improved radiologists' average accuracy (0.707 vs. 0.811, p<.001) for image review.
evidence.sample_unit: not specified (training n=2566, internal validation n=642, external validation n=717 and 493, prospective n=472)

evidence.title: Multimodal artificial intelligence for subepithelial lesion classification and characterization: a multicenter comparative study (with video)
evidence.venue: BMC medical informatics and decision making
evidence.outcome: Standalone AI diagnostic accuracy versus endoscopists without AI
evidence.effect: Model accuracy 96.35% vs endoscopists 63.87-86.13% (p<0.001); treatment decision accuracy 96.35% vs 78.47-86.13%. Standalone comparison only; no assistance condition tested.
evidence.quote: The ECMAI-WME model significantly outperformed endoscopists in diagnostic accuracy (96.35% vs. 63.87-86.13%, p < 0.001) and treatment decision-making accuracy (96.35% vs. 78.47-86.13%, p < 0.001).

evidence.title: Surgeon, Trainee, or GPT? A Blinded Multicentric Study of AI-Augmented Operative Notes
evidence.outcome: Human-AI versus human-only note performance
evidence.effect: Hybrid attending-plus-GPT notes had the highest average domain scores and 79% “as is” approval, outperforming all other groups.
evidence.quote: Hybrid notes written by an attending surgeon with GPT assistance received the highest average domain scores and the highest "as is" approval rate (79%), outperforming all other groups.

evidence.title: Enhancing knee MRI bone marrow lesion detection with artificial intelligence: An external validation study
evidence.venue: Research in diagnostic and interventional imaging
evidence.outcome: Reader sensitivity, specificity and reading time for bone marrow edema with versus without AI assistance
evidence.effect: Sensitivity rose from 79.3% to 85.4% and specificity from 88.9% to 93.9% with AI; reading time fell 42% (0.66 min per exam).
evidence.quote: AI significantly increased the sensitivity and specificity of bone marrow edema detection for general radiologists and shortened the reading process.

evidence.title: Large language model as clinical decision support system augments medication safety in 16 clinical specialties
evidence.outcome: Error identification accuracy for pharmacists with vs without LLM CDSS vs LLM alone
evidence.effect: Co-pilot accuracy 61% (SD 17.7) vs human alone 46% (SD 21.1), a 32.6% increase; overall ANOVA across modes not significant (p=0.38).
evidence.quote: The mean accuracy in identifying DRPs increased by 32.6% in co-pilot mode when compared against human alone (61%, SD 17.7 vs. 46%, SD 21.1).
evidence.sample_unit: simulated prescribing error scenarios (40 vignettes) reviewed by 6 pharmacists

evidence.title: Evaluation of a commercial deep-learning-based contouring software for CT-based gynecological brachytherapy
evidence.outcome: Interobserver agreement and contouring time, AI-assisted versus manual contouring by radiation oncologists
evidence.effect: AI-assisted interobserver agreement was better than manual for all organs and metrics; median contouring time 14.8 vs 6.9 minutes/patient (p < 0.001).
evidence.quote: AI-assisted interobserver agreement was better than manual interobserver agreement for all organs and metrics.

evidence.title: Application of Large Language Models in TN Staging and Treatment Response Evaluation for Patients With Nasopharyngeal Carcinoma: A Comparative Performance Analysis of ChatGPT-4o-Latest and DeepSeek-V3-0324
evidence.venue: Journal of magnetic resonance imaging : JMRI
evidence.outcome: Radiologist efficiency and performance with versus without LLM assistance
evidence.effect: Four radiologists assessed 68 cases with and without LLM assistance; significant time-efficiency improvements across all radiologists with LLM assistance (p < 0.001); diagnostic consistency may improve, especially for junior clinicians.
evidence.quote: Significant improvements in time efficiency were observed across all radiologists with LLM assistance (p < 0.001).
evidence.sample_unit: patients (831 reports) in test set; 68 cases in reader study

evidence.title: AI-Based System for Analysis of Electron Microscope Images in Glomerular Disease
evidence.outcome: Clinician diagnostic accuracy with versus without AI assistance on TEM images
evidence.effect: TEM-AID accuracy 0.886 (95% CI, 0.859-0.912) exceeded clinicians' unaided performance; clinicians' accuracy improved by a mean (SD) of 11.7% (5.2%) with TEM-AID.
evidence.quote: Clinicians' accuracy improved by a mean (SD) of 11.7% (5.2%) when they used TEM-AID.

evidence.title: Performance of Large Language Models in Diagnosing Rare Hematologic Diseases and the Impact of Their Diagnostic Outputs on Physicians: Combined Retrospective and Prospective Study
evidence.outcome: Physician diagnostic accuracy with versus without LLM assistance, and effect of biased LLM outputs
evidence.effect: LLMs significantly improved diagnostic accuracy of less-experienced physicians; no significant benefit for specialists. When LLMs gave biased responses, physician performance often failed to improve or declined.
evidence.quote: In the prospective phase, LLMs significantly improved the diagnostic accuracy of less-experienced physicians; no significant benefit was observed for specialists.
evidence.sample_unit: nonpublic real-world admission records (retrospective phase); 28 physicians diagnosing 5 cases each (prospective phase)

evidence.title: Development of a multi-task deep learning system for classification of nine common knee abnormalities on MRI: a large-scale, multicentre, stepwise validation study
evidence.outcome: Radiologist accuracy and reading time with versus without DLS assistance (randomised comparative study)
evidence.effect: DLS-assisted junior and senior radiologists had higher accuracy (difference 4.8-8.8% and 4.2-8.2%, all p<0.05) and reduced reading time (by 35.5 and 30.7 s, all p<0.05) vs control.
evidence.quote: For step 3, the randomised comparative study demonstrated that the junior and senior radiologists in the DLS-assisted group achieved significantly higher accuracy (difference of 4.8-8.8% and 4.2-8.2%, all p < 0.05) and reduced reading time (by 35.5 and 30.7 s, all p < 0.05) compared to the control group for nine knee abnormalities.

evidence.title: Large Language Model Assistant for Emergency Department Discharge Documentation
evidence.outcome: Note quality and writing time for physicians with versus without LLM assistance
evidence.effect: LLM-assisted notes scored higher than manual notes on all 4C metrics (all P<.001); median writing time fell from 69.5 to 32.0 seconds.
evidence.quote: The median documentation time per note dropped from 69.5 (95% CI, 65.5-78.0) seconds for manual notes to 32.0 (95% CI, 29.5-36.0) seconds for LLM-assisted notes (P < .001).

evidence.title: Evaluating human-in-the-loop strategies for artificial intelligence-enabled translation of patient discharge instructions: a multidisciplinary analysis
evidence.outcome: Preference and quality of AI-only vs human-in-the-loop vs professional translation, and time to completion
evidence.effect: Human-in-the-loop most preferred (46.5% vs 28.4% professional) and faster (7.1 vs 16.8 min, p<0.001); ChatGPT-4o least preferred in most languages.
evidence.quote: Across all languages, the mean time required to produce each translation was significantly faster for human-in-the-loop than professional translations (7.1 [95% CI 5.4–8.8] vs 16.8 [13.7–19.9] min, p < 0.001).
evidence.sample_unit: evaluators (12 linguists, 16 clinicians, 14 family caregivers) rating 20 discharge instruction texts translated into 6 languages

evidence.title: Malignancy prediction for calcified thyroid nodules using deep learning based on ultrasound dynamic videos
evidence.venue: Cancer imaging : the official publication of the International Cancer Imaging Society
evidence.outcome: Radiologist diagnostic accuracy with versus without AI assistance on external cohort
evidence.effect: With model assistance, radiologists' diagnostic accuracy improved by 16.9% (junior) and 11.1% (senior) in the external cohort; model AUROC 0.916 vs radiologists 0.638.
evidence.quote: Additionally, with the assistance of the optimized model, radiologists' diagnostic accuracy improved by 16.9% (junior) and 11.1% (senior) in the external cohort.

evidence.title: Application of AI-assisted magnifying colonoscopy system in the diagnosis of colorectal tumors: a multicenter exploratory diagnostic study
evidence.outcome: Endoscopist diagnostic accuracy with versus without AI assistance, by experience level
evidence.effect: Junior endoscopists improved accuracy from 0.866 to 0.951 after AADM assistance (P < 0.01); AADM alone 0.938 vs junior 0.866 (P<0.05), comparable to senior 0.937.
evidence.quote: Additionally, junior endoscopists significantly improved their accuracy from 0.866 to 0.951 after receiving assistance from the AADM (P < 0.01).

evidence.title: Uncertainty-aware large language models for explainable disease diagnosis
evidence.outcome: Expert uncertainty recognition and explanation with versus without ConfiDx assistance
evidence.effect: ConfiDx-assisted experts outperformed standalone experts by 10.7% in uncertainty recognition and 26% in uncertainty explanation.
evidence.quote: Moreover, ConfiDx-assisted experts outperformed standalone experts by 10.7% in uncertainty recognition and 26% in uncertainty explanation, underscoring its substantial potential to improve clinical decision-making.

evidence.title: Evaluating ChatGPT-4o as an Educational Support Tool for the Emergency Management of Dental Trauma: Randomized Controlled Study Among Students
evidence.outcome: Student exam accuracy and time with chatbot vs textbook, app, or no support tool
evidence.effect: All support tools improved accuracy vs control (P<.05); ChatGPT-4o mean accuracy 86.40% (SD 6.38%); chatbot and app groups needed significantly less time than textbook group (P<.05).
evidence.quote: All support tools led to a significantly higher accuracy compared with the control group (P<.05), with mean accuracies of 87.47% (SD 5.63%), 86.40% (SD 5.19%), and 86.40% (SD 6.38%) for the textbook, the AcciDent app, and ChatGPT-4o, respectively.

evidence.title: Impact of AI on Breast Cancer Detection Rates in Mammography by Radiologists of Varying Experience Levels in Singapore: Preliminary Comparative Study
evidence.outcome: Radiologist AUROC with versus without AI assistance in mammography reading
evidence.effect: AUROC rose in junior residents (0.84 to 0.86; P=.38) and senior residents (0.85 to 0.88; P=.13). Senior residents approached consultant-level performance (difference 0.02; P=.051).
evidence.quote: With AI assistance, AUROC improved among junior residents (from 0.84 to 0.86; P=.38) and senior residents (from 0.85 to 0.88; P=.13), with senior residents approaching consultant-level performance (AUROC difference 0.02; P=.051).

evidence.title: AI assistance improves reader agreement in digital mammography: A multireader crossover study of general and breast subspecialty radiologists
evidence.outcome: Reader agreement with gold standard with vs without AI assistance in multireader crossover
evidence.effect: AI assistance significantly improved agreement with the gold standard for general and subspecialty radiologists; general radiologists' Kappa for BI-RADS breast density rose from 50.01% to 81.38% with AI.
evidence.quote: AI assistance significantly improved agreement with the gold standard for both general and breast subspecialty radiologists.

evidence.title: Digital Pathology with AI for Cervical Biopsies: Diagnostic Accuracy at the CIN2+ Threshold
evidence.outcome: CIN2+ calling with vs without AI assistance for the same pathologist
evidence.effect: EE + P2 identified 69 CIN2+ vs P2 alone 70; agreement with P2-digital 90.7% (κ 0.79) for EE+P2 vs 88.7% (κ 0.74) for EE alone; P1 sensitivity 83.8% vs AI-assisted reference; no significant shift (p=1.00).
evidence.quote: These findings indicate that, for the high-volume expert reader, the AI-assisted workflow (EE + P2) did not significantly alter the overall CIN2+ calling rate relative to unaided digital review, but rather redistributed a small number of borderline cases in both directions.

evidence.title: Impact of AI recommendation correctness on diagnostic accuracy in clinical decision-making
evidence.outcome: Clinician diagnostic accuracy with versus without AI support, assessing overreliance
evidence.effect: Overall effect of introducing AI was equivocal versus baseline, with differential effect by AI correctness (OR = 10.0 when correct; reduced accuracy when incorrect).
evidence.quote: The overall effect of introducing AI was equivocal compared to baseline, however, there was a differential effect whether the recommendation was correct or wrong.

evidence.title: Deep Learning for Coronary Stenosis Detection in Heavily Calcified Plaques at Coronary CT Angiography: A Stepwise, Multicenter Study
evidence.outcome: Radiologist diagnostic performance with versus without DL assistance in reader study
evidence.effect: DL assistance improved radiologist specificity by 7%-11% (P < .001) with improving AUC and increased interreader agreement (Δκ = 0.155-0.228; P < .05).
evidence.quote: In external testing dataset 2, DL assistance improved radiologist specificity by 7%-11% (P < .001) with improving AUC and increased interreader agreement (Δκ = 0.155-0.228; P < .05).
evidence.sample_unit: CCTA examinations (development); external tests 442, 120, and 150 examinations

evidence.title: Evaluating Retrieval-Augmented Generation-Large Language Models for Infective Endocarditis Prophylaxis: Clinical Accuracy and Efficiency
evidence.outcome: Human performance with and without LLM assistance in intended deployment mode
evidence.effect: Postgraduate scores 85.0% to 86.4% (nonsignificant); undergraduates 82.9% to 79.3% (four of five decreased); all took longer with LLM.
evidence.quote: For undergraduate students, four out of five participants showed a decrease in their scores during the second round of the questionnaire, resulting in a nonsignificant drop from 82.9% ± 6.4 to 79.3% ± 4.67.
evidence.sample_unit: questions (true/false, 5 runs per model); plus 10 dental students in pilot

evidence.title: Comparative Performance of ChatGPT-4o, Grok-3, and Claude 3.7 Sonnet in Differentiating Cerebellopontine Angle Schwannomas and Meningiomas: A Pilot Study of Visual Versus Text-Based Diagnostic Prompting
evidence.venue: Journal of imaging informatics in medicine
evidence.outcome: LLM diagnostic accuracy versus radiologists across input types (raw images, expert or resident structured features)
evidence.effect: With expert features GPT-4o reached 94.3% vs expert 92.5% (p=1.000) and resident 79.2% (p=0.021); with raw images LLMs 18.9-52.8%, significantly worse than radiologists (p<0.05). Not tested as human-AI teams.
evidence.quote: With expert-derived structured features, LLMs achieved high accuracy (86.8-94.3%), with GPT-4o reaching 94.3% (95%CI 84.6-98.1%), matching the expert neuroradiologist (92.5%, 95%CI 82.1-97.0%, p = 1.000) and significantly outperforming the resident (79.2%, p = 0.021).

evidence.title: Artificial intelligence for personalized management of vestibular schwannoma: a multidisciplinary clinical implementation study
evidence.outcome: Preparation and discussion time in simulated multidisciplinary meetings with versus without AI-assisted reports
evidence.effect: AI reports lengthened neuroradiologist preparation (2 min 54 s vs 2 min 36 s per case) but shortened discussion (1 min 15 s vs 1 min 21 s per case, P < .01).
evidence.quote: However, the computer-assisted simulated MDTM approach significantly improved (P < .01) MDTM efficiency, with shorter discussion times per patient (1 min 15 s [ ± 0 min and 28 s] per case) compared to standard simulated MDTM (1 min 21 s [ ± 0 min and 44 s] per case).

evidence.title: Quantifying the impact of a computer-aided diagnostic score on the clinical diagnosis of functional seizures
evidence.outcome: Reader diagnostic accuracy with versus without FSLS; overreliance assessed via change analysis
evidence.effect: Groups containing 66% of readers improved accuracy by 12%-15% with FSLS (p<.05); other groups had no net change (p>.75); no reader adopted FSLS errors uncritically.
evidence.quote: Machine learning‐assisted identification with the FSLS improved the performance of groups containing 66% of readers by 12%–15%, but other readers could not effectively identify when to change their diagnosis based on the FSLS.

evidence.title: Assessing the communication gap between AI models and healthcare professionals: Explainability, utility and trust in AI-driven clinical decision-making
evidence.outcome: Human-AI team decisions with and without explanation, including overreliance on incorrect model recommendations
evidence.effect: Lowest concordance in cases where CORONET recommended wrong action; 35% (CS) and 52% (CS+Exp) of HCPs overrode incorrect discharge recommendations.
evidence.quote: Only 35% (CS scenario) and 52% (CS+Ex) HCPs took that critical perspective over the model.

evidence.title: Direct deep learning analysis of three-dimensional automated breast ultrasound videos with reading mode optimization for breast cancer diagnosis
evidence.outcome: Radiologist diagnostic performance with vs without AI assistance (independent vs second vs concurrent reading)
evidence.effect: Experienced AUC 0.83 to 0.90 (P<0.001); novice AUC 0.68 to 0.84 (second) and 0.85 (concurrent), P<0.001; specificity in novices 57.4% to 82.7%/83.3%.
evidence.quote: Similarly, novice radiologists also showed significantly improved AUC (second-reading: 0.84 vs. 0.68, P<0.001; concurrent-reading: 0.85 vs. 0.68, P<0.001), sensitivity (second-reading: 87.5% vs. 79.2%, P<0.001; concurrent-reading: 88.1% vs. 79.2%, P<0.001), and specificity (second-reading: 82.7% vs. 57.4%, P<0.001; concurrent-reading: 83.3% vs. 57.4%, P<0.001) compared with independent-reading.
evidence.sample_unit: patients (test set; 547 total, read by 6 radiologists)

evidence.title: Effect of ChatGPT-Assisted Reflective Reasoning on Guideline-Concordant Procedural Decision-Making Among Early-Career Interventional Radiologists
evidence.outcome: Guideline-concordant decisions by radiologists with vs without ChatGPT assistance
evidence.effect: Mean detailed compliance score rose from 1.697 to 1.900; minimal compliance from 90.89% to 98.70%; 30 scenario-level corrections (McNemar χ² = 27.03; p < 0.0001).
evidence.quote: ChatGPT-assisted reflective reasoning significantly improved guideline-concordant decision-making.
evidence.sample_unit: simulated clinical scenarios (each completed twice by 3 early-career radiologists)

evidence.title: A large language model for complex cardiology care
evidence.outcome: Subspecialist preference and error rates for cardiologists with versus without AI assistance
evidence.effect: AMIE-assisted assessments preferred 46.7% vs 32.7% for cardiologists alone (P = 0.02); clinically significant errors 13.1% with AMIE vs 24.3% alone (P = 0.033).
evidence.quote: Subspecialists also quantified errors, extra and missing content, reasoning and potential bias.

evidence.title: Clinical Impact of Artificial Intelligence-Augmented Lymph Node Evaluation in Metastatic Gastric, Colorectal, and Breast Cancer
evidence.outcome: Pathologist sensitivity, specificity, and review time with versus without AI assistance
evidence.effect: AI assistance increased sensitivity from 91.8%-93.9% to 95.9% for all pathologists; specificity remained 97.0%-98.9%; review time decreased by up to 78% for some cancer types.
evidence.quote: AI assistance increased sensitivity-which ranged from 91.8% to 93.9%-to 95.9% for all pathologists, while specificity remained high (97.0%-98.9%).
evidence.sample_unit: whole slide images (from 95 patients), read by 3 pathologists with and without AI

evidence.title: Success and failure of human-AI collaboration in clinical reasoning: An experimental study on challenging real-world cases
evidence.outcome: Diagnostic accuracy of clinicians with vs without LLM collaboration compared with LLM-only accuracy
evidence.effect: Accuracy rose from 0.45 to 0.60 with HAC (P<0.001); 20% of participants declined; HAC mean stayed below LLM-only accuracy (0.70).
evidence.quote: HAC significantly improved mean accuracy compared to the human-only condition (from 0.45 to 0.60, P < 0.001), although 20% of participants showed a decline in performance and the mean remained below the LLM-only accuracy (0.70).
evidence.sample_unit: participants (10 ophthalmologists, 10 residents, 10 senior medical students), each completing 30 cases

evidence.title: Artificial intelligence-assisted training for rib fracture interpretation: a prospective study in undergraduate medical students
evidence.venue: World journal of emergency surgery : WJES
evidence.outcome: Reader diagnostic performance with vs without AI heatmap assistance, and overreliance assessment
evidence.effect: AI assistance (S2) improved accuracy 26.7%, sensitivity 41.0%, specificity 25.1%, F1 35.6%, precision 31.4% (all p<0.01); agreement with AI on AI-misclassified cases rose (S1 vs S2 p=0.037), suggesting automation bias.
evidence.quote: Significant improvements were observed during the S2 using AI heatmapping, with a 26.7% increase in accuracy, 25.1% in specificity, 41.0% in sensitivity, 35.6% in F1 score, and 31.4% in precision (all p-values < 0.01).

evidence.title: Prospective quantitative analysis of hyperparameter and input optimization in GPT-5: comparative contribution to radiologist performance in abdominal radiology
evidence.outcome: Radiologist diagnostic accuracy with vs without GPT-5 assistance
evidence.effect: R1/R2 accuracy rose from 73%/71% unassisted to 87%/86% with browser GPT-5 and 94%/94% with optimal-settings GPT-5 (P=0.001; P=0.031/0.028). Overreliance not assessed.
evidence.quote: With browser-based GPT-5 assistance, their accuracy significantly improved to 87% (75/86; 95% CI: 79%–94%) and 86% (74/86; 95% CI: 78%–93%), respectively ( P = 0.001, P = 0.001).

evidence.title: Evolving Consultation: Enhancing Ophthalmic Diagnostic Performance Using Large Language Model
evidence.outcome: Clinician scores with versus without LLM assistance on coherency, factuality, comprehensiveness, safety
evidence.effect: Assistance improved coherency, comprehensiveness, and safety in both groups (all P<0.001); factuality showed no significant improvement (P=0.114 and 0.839); variability in factuality and safety increased.
evidence.quote: Assistance from ChatGPT-4o significantly improved evaluation scores for coherency, comprehensiveness, and safety among both residents and board-certified ophthalmologists (all, P < 0.001).
evidence.sample_unit: ophthalmologists (10 residents, 10 board-certified) answering 10 clinical scenarios

evidence.title: Explainable deep learning framework incorporating medical knowledge for insulin titration in diabetes
evidence.outcome: Clinician insulin titration accuracy and confidence with versus without STII-DIL assistance
evidence.effect: Accuracy significantly improved for junior clinicians with STII-DIL assistance, while senior clinicians showed minimal change; both groups reported increased confidence.
evidence.quote: An AI-human collaboration study revealed that insulin titration accuracy significantly improved for junior clinicians with STII-DIL assistance, while senior clinicians showed minimal change.
evidence.sample_unit: inpatients with T2DM (1,275 internal, 292 external EHR cohort)

evidence.title: Improving Trauma Triage Accuracy with Large Language Models: A Comparison to Human Expert Decisions
evidence.venue: Journal of the American College of Surgeons
evidence.outcome: Trauma surgeon triage accuracy before vs after LLM exposure, compared with standalone LLM accuracy
evidence.effect: Human accuracy rose from 73.7% to 75.8% after LLM exposure (p = 0.04, Bonferroni p = 0.12); odds ratio 2.57 (95% CI 1.39 to 6.83). Standalone LLM accuracy was 83.5% vs 78.9% for humans.
evidence.quote: In prospective evaluation, human triage accuracy improved after LLM exposure (73.7% [69.8 to 77.2]) to 75.8% ([71.9 to 79.2], p = 0.04, Bonferroni p = 0.12), significantly improving the odds of a correct triage decision (odds ratio 2.57, 95% CI 1.39 to 6.83, p < 0.01).

evidence.title: Evaluating the diagnostic performance of artificial intelligence-assisted decision-making software for pulmonary nodules in a resource-limited setting
evidence.outcome: Reader diagnostic performance (AUC) with versus without AI assistance
evidence.effect: Average AUC rose from 0.78 to 0.89 (mean difference 0.11, 95% CI 0.08, 0.14) with AI-assisted DMS; improvements consistent across experience levels and specialties.
evidence.quote: AI-assisted DMS significantly improved readers' diagnostic performance, with the average AUC increasing from 0.78 to 0.89 (mean difference: 0.11, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.08, 0.14).
evidence.sample_unit: chest CT scans (enriched; read by 6 physicians)

evidence.title: Artificial intelligence assistance improves endoscopist accuracy for gastric cancer dysplasia and intestinal metaplasia
evidence.outcome: Endoscopist diagnostic accuracy and AUC with vs without AI assistance on still images and videos
evidence.effect: Reader accuracy rose from 74.92% to 86.66% (M1, AUC 0.742 to 0.860) and to 86.81% (M2, AUC 0.796 to 0.900), all p<0.05. Stand-alone AI accuracy was 91.31% (M1) and 92.51% (M2).
evidence.quote: With AI assistance, overall reader accuracy increased from 74.92% to 86.66% in M1 (AUC 0.742 to 0.860) and likewise from 74.92% to 86.81% in M2 (AUC 0.796 to 0.900); all p < 0.05.
evidence.sample_unit: cases (still images and video clips) read by 6 in-training endoscopists

evidence.title: Benchmarking a deep learning model against healthcare practitioners for hip fracture detection in the emergency department
evidence.outcome: Junior doctor performance with versus without DL model outputs
evidence.effect: No significant difference in performance between DL model and ED junior doctors reading independently or with DL support.
evidence.quote: There was no significant difference in performance between the DL model and ED junior doctors, who read the original radiographs independently or with support from the DL model.

evidence.title: Digitally Assisted Clinical Decision-Making in Traditional Chinese Medicine: Comparative Study of 5 Large Language Models
evidence.outcome: Decision quality and time for physicians with vs without LLM assistance
evidence.effect: Human-AI collaboration scored 33.62 vs physician-only 28.97 (P<.001), 66.1% time reduction (162.6 s vs 479.2 s); AI-only 33.80, not different from collaboration (P=.79).
evidence.quote: Pairwise comparisons revealed that human-AI collaboration significantly outperformed physician-only decision-making (paired t 49 =6.603, Cohen d =0.943; P< .001), representing a 116.1% quality improvement.
evidence.sample_unit: TCM practitioners (plus 160 exam questions, 30 cases, 5 clinical cases for human-AI comparison)

evidence.title: Integrating Large Language Models Into Trauma Education for Medical Students: Randomized Controlled Pilot Trial
evidence.outcome: Decision accuracy and speed of students with vs without LLM access in trauma simulation
evidence.effect: LLM support did not enhance decision accuracy or speed; longer response times in some complex cases; teamwork median 3.5 vs 5.0 (P=.08); confidence gains larger without LLM (P=.02).
evidence.quote: LLM support did not enhance the decision accuracy or speed and was associated with longer response times in some complex cases.
languages: non-English (prompting language not specified in abstract)

evidence.title: From tool to teammate in a randomized controlled trial of clinician-AI collaborative workflows for diagnosis
evidence.outcome: Clinician diagnostic score with AI first, AI second, versus conventional resources; AI alone
evidence.effect: Conventional 75% vs AI first 85% (mean diff 9.9%, p=0.00039) and AI second 82% (6.8%, p=3.3e-6); clinicians with AI not significantly different from AI alone.
evidence.quote: Clinicians using conventional resources only had a significantly lower overall score (75%) than either AI arm, with the clinicians’ using AI as a first opinion (85%, p = 0.00039, mean difference=9.9%, 95% CI = 4.7–15%), or AI as a second opinion (82%, p = 3.3e−6, mean difference=6.8%, 95% CI = 4.0–9.6%).

evidence.title: Large language models enhance diagnostic reasoning of medical students in rheumatology: a randomized controlled trial
evidence.outcome: Correct top diagnosis: students with LLM vs without, and vs LLM alone
evidence.effect: LLM group 77.5% vs controls 32.4% (aOR 7.0, 95% CI 3.8–14.4; P<.001); also exceeded LLM-only performance (77.5% vs. 71.6%).
evidence.quote: The LLM group identified the correct top diagnosis more often than controls (77.5% vs. 32.4%), yielding an adjusted odds ratio of 7.0 (95% CI 3.8–14.4; P<.001), and also exceeded LLM-only performance (77.5% vs. 71.6%).

evidence.title: Effect of large language model on diagnostic accuracy and clinical completeness among nephrology fellows managing transplant infection
evidence.outcome: Fellow accuracy, completeness, and time-to-answer with versus without LLM assistance on vignettes
evidence.effect: Median accuracy rose from 72% to 85.5% (Δ +13.0%, p<0.001); completeness 1.9 to 2.5 (p<0.001); time-to-answer 7.1 to 5.9 min (p=0.002).
evidence.quote: Median accuracy increased from 72% (65·5-78·5) in the unaided arm to 85·5% (79·0-91·0) in the aided arm with Δ =  + 13·0%, p-value < 0·001.

evidence.title: External validation of a commercial AI system for pulmonary embolism detection on chest CTPA: a multicenter study
evidence.outcome: Diagnostic AUC and errors for radiologists with vs without AI, and AI alone
evidence.effect: Combined AUC 0.928-0.934 vs manual 0.888-0.914 and AI alone 0.807-0.810; errors 7 combined vs 29 manual vs 43 AI alone; overall manual vs combined P=0.0427.
evidence.quote: The combined radiologist + AI approach resulted in only 7 diagnostic errors (2 false-negative and 5 false-positive cases), representing a 75.9% reduction in errors compared to AI alone and a 75.9% reduction compared to radiologists alone.

evidence.title: The Role of Artificial Intelligence and Professional Expertise in Adapted Physical Activity Prescription for Orthopedic Rehabilitation
evidence.venue: Journal of functional morphology and kinesiology
evidence.outcome: Perceived protocol quality: novice with AI vs AI alone vs expert, blinded ratings
evidence.effect: EP scored highest, NAI intermediate, AI alone lowest across all five conditions (e.g., scoliosis 4.35/3.96/3.38; Friedman p<0.001); NAI vs AI significant except osteoporosis (p=0.362).
evidence.quote: Across all investigated pathologies, the APA protocols designed by the EP consistently achieved the highest overall evaluation scores, followed by the protocols developed by the NAI, while the AI protocols received the lowest scores.

evidence.title: A prospective multicenter trial of deep learning auto-segmentation for organs at risk in thoracic radiotherapy
evidence.outcome: Contour accuracy for manual vs AI-only vs physician-plus-AI delineation
evidence.effect: Mean vDSC 0.857 manual, 0.896 AI, 0.902 AI-assisted; HD95 8.01, 5.62, 5.20 mm; sequential significant improvement (p<0.0001); time median 10.0 vs 55.0 min.
evidence.quote: These data show a sequential and significant improvement in accuracy from manual, to AI, and to AI-assisted delineation ( p < 0.0001), a trend that was further supported by sDSC ( p < 0.0001) (Supplementary Fig. 3 ).

evidence.title: Comparative performance of LLMs and machine learning in predicting complications after percutaneous kyphoplasty for osteoporotic vertebral compression fractures
evidence.outcome: Surgeon prediction performance with versus without LLM predictions and explanations
evidence.effect: BCL: surgeon F1 rose from 0.675-0.684 to 0.724-0.752; NVF: subtle contrary changes, Surgeon 1 F1 0.310 to 0.370-0.409, Surgeon 2 0.322 to 0.308-0.315.
evidence.quote: After consultation of the predictions and interpretations from either LLMs, their performances showed subtle but contrary change that F1 score slightly increased to 0.370–0.409 and MCC to 0.185–0.266 for Surgeon 1 , while the numbers slightly decreased to 0.308–0.315 and 0.061–0.077 for Surgeon 2 .
evidence.sample_unit: prospective test samples for BCL prediction (116 for NVF)

evidence.title: The effects of multitype prompt engineering for large language models in hypertension treatment decisions
evidence.outcome: Physician accuracy with vs without LLM assistance, including poor-LLM assistance (overreliance)
evidence.effect: Optimal LLM raised physician accuracy (community 73.4% to 82.5%; county 84.0% to 87.9%; teaching 91.5% to 92.0%); worst LLM lowered accuracy below baseline, inappropriate regimens 26.6% to 35.2%.
evidence.quote: The worst LLM configurations decreased physician performance below baseline, increasing inappropriate regimen rates from 26.6% to 35.2% across all levels.

evidence.title: Transforming adnexal mass assessment: how large language model improve ovarian-adnexal reporting and data system interpretation and sonographer performance
