evidence.outcome: Reader diagnostic performance (AUC) and agreement with vs without LLM assistance, junior vs senior
evidence.effect: Juniors with LLM: weighted κ ≥ 0.85, mean ΔAUC = 0.10 (p = 0.06, non-significant); seniors ΔAUC = 0.01 (p = 0.22). Gains reflect reliance on LLM rather than independent skill.
evidence.quote: In contrast, senior readers showed stable performance (mean ΔAUC = 0.01; p = 0.22).
evidence.sample_unit: lesions (302 patients); 150-lesion subset read by 4 readers

evidence.title: Patch-to-slide fusion deep learning model for histological diagnosis of early pregnancy loss including hydatidiform mole
evidence.outcome: Pathologist diagnostic performance with versus without AI assistance
evidence.effect: AI-assisted diagnosis significantly improved pathologist performance (p < 0.05).
evidence.quote: AI-assisted diagnosis significantly improved pathologist performance (p < 0.05).

evidence.title: Bolstering the Performance of Breast Radiologists with AI-CAD in Mammography: A Multireader Study
evidence.outcome: Radiologist diagnostic performance and reading time with vs without AI-CAD assistance
evidence.effect: AUC rose from 0.799 to 0.851 (p = 0.0151); specificity 77.0% to 88.4% (p = 0.03); sensitivity no significant difference; reading time 121.5 to 83.2 s per case (p < 0.001).
evidence.quote: AI-CAD assistance significantly improved diagnostic performance, with the average area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (area under the curve [AUC]) increasing from 0.799 to 0.851 (p = 0.0151).

evidence.title: Colorectal cancer detection using noncontrast CT and deep learning: a multicenter and international cohort study
evidence.venue: Annals of oncology : official journal of the European Society for Medical Oncology
evidence.outcome: Radiologist CRC detection sensitivity and specificity with versus without AI assistance in reader study
evidence.effect: COCA improved CRC detection sensitivity by 20.4% and specificity by 5.4% compared with radiologists.
evidence.quote: COCA improved CRC detection sensitivity by 20.4% and specificity by 5.4% compared with radiologists.
evidence.sample_unit: consecutive patients in real-world cohorts (plus 2053 patients in external validation and 10 radiologists in reader study)

evidence.title: The effect of medical explanations from large language models on diagnostic accuracy in radiology
evidence.outcome: Radiologist diagnostic accuracy with vs without LLM support by explanation format; adherence/overreliance
evidence.effect: Chain-of-thought improved accuracy 12.2 pp vs control (P=0.001); standard output +5.0 pp (P=0.150) and differential diagnosis +2.5 pp (P=0.446) not significant vs control. Differential diagnosis group over-adhered to wrong advice (63.3-80.0%).
evidence.quote: Physicians in the chain-of-thought group performed best with a 12.2 percentage point improvement over the control group (95% CI = [5.3, 19.2], P = 0.001).

evidence.title: A pilot study on the impact of large language model assistance on the evaluation of complex medical living kidney donor candidates
evidence.outcome: Physician accuracy, justification quality and confidence with vs without LLM assistance

evidence.title: Automated detection of hyperdense artery sign on non-contrast CT for rapid identification of large vessel occlusion: a multicenter validation study

evidence.title: Multicenter validation and randomized crossover reader evaluation of deep learning-assisted tri-sequence three-dimensional MRI segmentation for hypopharyngeal tumor

evidence.title: AI assisted detection of large vessel occlusion on non-contrast CT: multinational validation and reader study
evidence.outcome: Clinician diagnostic performance with versus without AI assistance, including automation bias

evidence.quote: AI assistance significantly increased pooled AUC values from 0.718 to 0.852, sensitivity from 46.6% to 63.7%, and specificity from 91.9% to 94.9% (all P<0.001).

evidence.title: Evaluation of segmentation accuracy and the improvement of time effectiveness using deep learning-based segmentation in 177Lu-DOTATATE dosimetry
evidence.outcome: AI-corrected versus manual dosimetry time
evidence.effect: Reference/AI-corrected method: 47.0 [30.0-58.0] min vs manual 54.3 [49.5-67.0] min, p = 0.014.
evidence.quote: Dosimetry using the reference method took significantly less time than the manual approach (47.0 [30.0-58.0] min vs. 54.3 [49.5-67.0] min, p = 0.014).

evidence.title: Human-in-the-Loop Enhances Machine Learning Inference in Intraoperative Optical Coherence Tomography Glioma Imaging
evidence.outcome: Diagnostic accuracy/sensitivity of surgeons with AI segmentation maps versus AI alone and surgeons without AI
evidence.effect: HITL accuracy 94% [88-98], sensitivity 98% vs SVM alone accuracy 84%, sensitivity 83%; Gemini accuracy 90%, sensitivity 86%; structural scans without ML 80%. Surgeons overrode 9 of 13 AI false positives.
evidence.quote: Yet, human inference on the segmented scans achieved a superior, statistically significant accuracy of 94% [95% CI: 88–98%].

evidence.title: Evaluating cognitive biases in AI-assisted mammography interpretation: a simulation reader study of explainable AI across radiologist experience levels
evidence.outcome: Reader diagnostic accuracy unaided versus AI-assisted with XAI, and overreliance on AI
evidence.effect: On non-manipulated cases, accuracy improved from 724/840 (86.2%) unaided to 757/840 (90.1%) with AI + XAI; bias present when AI was misleading.
evidence.quote: On the non-manipulated subset, diagnostic accuracy improved from 724/840 (86.2%) in the unaided phase to 757/840 (90.1%) in the AI + XAI phase.

evidence.title: Quality assessment of radiographs through AI-driven feedback: A randomized comparative study on radiographer response in lateral knee radiographs
evidence.outcome: Radiographer accept/reject performance with versus without AI annotations; overreliance on incorrect AI
evidence.effect: Sensitivity identical with and without AI (0.64); no significant differences in specificity, PPV, NPV; inter-reader agreement lower with AI (AC 0.233 vs 0.374); false AI feedback reduced sensitivity and specificity in repeated cases.
evidence.quote: Radiographers' sensitivity was identical with and without AI support (0.64), with no significant differences in specificity, PPV, or NPV.

evidence.title: Bilateral disease in the classic subtype of papillary thyroid carcinoma: clinical significance and development of an artificial intelligence-based multimodal prediction model
evidence.outcome: Radiologist diagnostic accuracy with versus without AI model assistance across experience levels
evidence.effect: In the external validation group of 120 patients, Model D significantly improved diagnostic accuracy across all radiologist experience levels, with junior radiologists improving most (+20.9%).
evidence.quote: In the external validation group of 120 patients, Model D's implementation significantly improved diagnostic accuracy across all radiologist experience levels, with junior radiologists benefiting most substantially (+20.9% improvement).

evidence.title: Toward Long-Term Visual Field Appearance Forecasting Using Artificial Intelligence for Ophthalmic Education and Diagnosis
evidence.outcome: Resident glaucoma progression rating error, confidence, and reaction time with versus without AI forecasts
evidence.effect: Global MAE showed minor differences with vs without AI forecasts; heterogeneous patient-specific impacts; residents more conservative and more confident with AI; reaction times comparable.
evidence.quote: Globally, MAE for GP ratings with and without AI forecasts show minor differences.

evidence.title: Multi-label dynamic diagnosis of pancreatic diseases using AI-enhanced endoscopic ultrasound: a multi-cohort real-world study
evidence.outcome: Endoscopist diagnostic performance with versus without AI-Paradise assistance in computer-assisted diagnostic test
evidence.effect: Novice endoscopists significantly improved; best-performing novice increased from 39.4 to 57.4% (p < 0.0001).
evidence.quote: In CADT, performance of novice endoscopists significantly improved, with the best-performing novice achieving an increase from 39·4 to 57·4% (p < 0·0001).

evidence.title: Evaluation of Large Language Models in Infectious Disease Decision-Making: From Examination to Clinical Practice
evidence.outcome: Doctor decision quality with versus without LLM assistance, and LLM alone (accuracy, completeness)
evidence.effect: Completeness rose from 4.50 (doctors alone) to 4.90 with LLM support (p=0.0015 vs doctors; p=0.0010 vs LLMs alone); accuracy 4.50 to 4.67, not significant (p=0.19).
evidence.quote: Post hoc analysis demonstrated that doctors supported by LLMs achieved significantly higher completeness scores compared with both the doctors alone ( p = 0.0015) and the LLMs alone ( p = 0.0010).

evidence.title: Non-invasive evaluation of muscle invasion and survival prognosis in bladder cancer using enhanced CT-based deep learning radiomics: a multi-center real-world cohort study
evidence.outcome: Urologist diagnostic sensitivity and accuracy with versus without AI assistance
evidence.effect: AI-assisted diagnostics significantly improved the sensitivity and accuracy of urologists, particularly among less experienced clinicians.
evidence.quote: AI-assisted diagnostics significantly improved the sensitivity and accuracy of urologists, particularly among less experienced clinicians.

evidence.title: YOLO26x-based automated fracture detection on radiographs and its impact on radiologist performance: A multi-reader multi-case study
evidence.outcome: Reader accuracy, agreement, and reading time with versus without model assistance
evidence.effect: Accuracy improved for two of three readers (RAD1 76.2% to 83.4%; RAD3 75.6% to 83.4%); Fleiss' kappa 0.432 to 0.642; beneficial decision changes 197 vs detrimental 104 across 1,500 reader-case pairs.
evidence.quote: Model-assisted reading significantly improved accuracy for two of three readers (RAD1: 76.2 % → 83.4 %, p = 0.001; RAD3: 75.6 % → 83.4 %, p < 0.001; Holm-corrected), with sensitivity gains of 2.4-16.4 percentage points.

evidence.title: Clinical Validation of a Generative AI System for Diagnosing Ampullary Lesions: A Multicenter Study
evidence.outcome: Endoscopist adenoma sensitivity with versus without CAD assistance in reader study
evidence.effect: CAD assistance raised adenoma sensitivity from 63.47% to 70.56% (p < 0.01), with improved predictive values; both expert and trainee endoscopists benefited and interobserver variability decreased.
evidence.quote: In the reader study, CAD assistance significantly increased adenoma sensitivity (63.47%-70.56%; p < 0.01), with corresponding improvements in predictive values.

evidence.title: Large-language-models for pediatric diagnosis: Performance evaluation using real-world clinical notes from common and rare cases
evidence.outcome: Human-AI complementarity: union accuracy of clinicians plus LLM versus clinicians alone
evidence.effect: Union accuracy with o1-preview was 94.3%, a 10-percentage-point uplift over clinicians alone.
evidence.quote: Human-Artificial intelligence complementarity analysis revealed 94.3% union accuracy with o1-preview, representing a 10-percentage-point uplift over clinicians alone.
evidence.sample_unit: real clinical cases (each queried three times per LLM; compared with 78 pediatric clinicians)

evidence.title: Med-Diet: evaluation of an LLM-based system for clinically guided nutrition care in chronic diseases
evidence.outcome: Nutritionist efficiency and expert-rated plan quality without versus with Med-Diet assistance
evidence.effect: Median time fell from 17.5 to 13.0 min (p < 0.05); accuracy, personalization, practicality and overall scores were higher in the Med-Diet-assisted group (adjusted p < 0.05). Overreliance was not assessed.
evidence.quote: Expert scores for accuracy, personalization, practicality, and overall recommendation were higher in the Med-Diet-assisted group (adjusted p < 0.05).

evidence.title: Clinical decision support in hematological malignancies using a case-grounded AI agent
evidence.outcome: Resident treatment-recommendation concordance with and without AI assistance
evidence.effect: Residents (n = 4) evaluated 30 cases. Unaided concordance was approximately 60%; HemaGuide-assisted residents achieved near-senior concordance and sometimes exceeded senior subspecialists. Overreliance was not assessed.
evidence.quote: Unaided residents matched the tumor board ground truth in approximately 60% of cases, whereas residents with HemaGuide support achieved near-senior concordance, and in some comparisons superior performance, relative to senior physicians assessing cases inside their primary disease expertise (Fig. 4e–g ).

evidence.title: Radiologist-Large Language Model Collaboration in Dermatologic Ultrasound Reporting: Evaluating the Clinical Utility of ChatGPT
evidence.venue: Studies in health technology and informatics
evidence.outcome: Diagnostic accuracy of radiologist alone, LLM alone, and radiologist plus LLM collaboration
evidence.effect: Diagnostic accuracy was highest in Condition 3 (83.2%), compared with Condition 1 (55.4%) and Condition 2 (26.2%) (p<0.001).
evidence.quote: Diagnostic accuracy was highest in Condition 3 (83.2%), compared with Condition 1 (55.4%) and Condition 2 (26.2%) (p<0.001).

evidence.title: Benchmarking large language models against practicing clinicians on psychopathological assessment
evidence.outcome: Accuracy of simulated disagreement resolutions with LLM or board-certified supervision versus unsupervised clinician selection
evidence.effect: In 2091 clinician pairs (35.5% disagreements), LLM and board-certified supervision gave more accurate resolutions than unsupervised random clinician selection (p < 0.0002).
evidence.quote: In post hoc simulated disagreement resolutions (2091 clinician pairs; 35.5% disagreements), LLM and board-certified supervision were associated with more accurate resolutions than unsupervised random clinician selection (p < 0.0002).
evidence.sample_unit: early-career clinicians (benchmark comparators); 10 LLMs rated transcripts of 3 simulated interviews across 100 AMDP items

evidence.title: Impact of an AI algorithm for multi-day prediction of incident atrial fibrillation on clinical decision-making: PROVISION-AF study
evidence.outcome: Physician AF risk discrimination with versus without AI assistance in simulated cases
evidence.effect: AI assistance improved physicians' AF risk discrimination (AUROC 0.573 to 0.650) and NPV (0.764 to 0.839); NRI 0.127 for non-AF cases, p < 0.001.
evidence.quote: AI assistance significantly improved physicians' AF risk discrimination (AUROC 0.573 to 0.650) and negative predictive value (0.764 to 0.839), with significant net reclassification improvement for non-AF cases (NRI 0.127, p < 0.001).

evidence.title: ConLymphNet: A Generalizable Region-Constrained Deep Learning Architecture for Precise Abdominal Lymph Node Segmentation Across Cancer Types
evidence.outcome: Radiologist detection and segmentation performance with versus without AI assistance
evidence.effect: AI assistance improved radiologists' performance significantly, particularly for less experienced readers (detection rate +20.2%, segmentation accuracy +13.0%, P < .001), while reducing false positives by 33.3%.
evidence.quote: AI assistance improved radiologists' performance significantly, particularly for less experienced readers (detection rate +20.2%, segmentation accuracy +13.0%, P < .001), while reducing false positives by 33.3%.

evidence.title: Real-world evaluation of medication recommendation workflows: Retrieval augmentation, physician-RAG collaborative workflow, and prescribing quality
evidence.outcome: Comparing physician alone, LLM alone, RAG alone, and physician-RAG collaboration against expert reference
evidence.effect: Physician-RAG had the highest CORE recall (1.000), precision (0.963), Jaccard (0.943) and lowest AVOID-hit rate (0.026); all-correct prescription rate 0.951 vs 0.945 physician and 0.494 base LLM.
evidence.quote: Prescription-parameter accuracy was highest in the Physician-RAG collaborative workflow (all-correct rate 0.951), compared with 0.948 for the Retrieval-augmented LLM workflow, 0.945 for the Physician workflow, and 0.494 for the Base LLM workflow.

evidence.title: Multimodal foundation model assistance for differentiating primary open-angle glaucoma in highly myopic eyes
evidence.outcome: Ophthalmologist diagnostic performance with versus without AI assistance in paired sequential reading
evidence.effect: Model AUC 0.911; mean sensitivity 68.0% unaided vs 75.3% AI-assisted, accuracy 74.2% vs 79.6%, specificity 91.3% in both phases; reader-level differences not significant after multiplicity adjustment.
evidence.quote: Reader-level diagnostic differences were not significant after multiplicity adjustment and were exploratory.
evidence.sample_unit: eye-level cases (from 149 patients) read by six ophthalmologists

evidence.title: Diagnostic Performance of Large Language Models for Orthopedic-Related Rare Diseases and Their Impact on Physicians' Diagnostic Accuracy: 2-Stage Comparative Evaluation Study Based on the Chinese Rare Disease Catalog
evidence.outcome: Physician diagnostic accuracy with versus without LLM assistance (2-stage workflow)
evidence.effect: Mean accuracy rose from 42.22% to 68.80% (intermediate) and 58.67% to 83.33% (senior); stage significantly associated with correctness (P<.001). Overreliance was not formally assessed.
evidence.quote: Before LLM assistance, mean physician-level accuracy was 42.22% for intermediate physicians and 58.67% for senior physicians; after assistance, it increased to 68.80% and 83.33%, respectively.
evidence.sample_unit: orthopedic physicians (27 intermediate, 15 senior) diagnosing 40 rare disease cases

evidence.title: Evaluating the Intermediate Suspicion Category in Thyroid Nodules With Artificial Intelligence Assistance: A Comparative Analysis of C-TIRADS, ACR-TIRADS, and American Thyroid Association Guidelines
evidence.venue: Journal of the American College of Radiology : JACR
evidence.outcome: Radiologist diagnostic accuracy with versus without AI assistance in intermediate suspicion nodules
evidence.effect: Radiologists' accuracy rose from 66.4%-71.4% without AI to 74.1%-79.4% with AI across three guidelines (P < .001).
evidence.quote: Radiologists' overall accuracy increased from 66.4% to 71.4% without AI to 74.1% to 79.4% with AI across all three guidelines (P < .001).

evidence.title: Development and Validation of a Machine Learning Classification Algorithm for Differentiating Frontotemporal Dementia from Alzheimer's Disease Using Automated Brain MRI Volumetry
evidence.outcome: Reader accuracy and interpretation time with versus without algorithm assistance
evidence.effect: Experienced readers maintained accuracy with significantly reduced reading time (p < 0.001) with algorithm assistance; the underexperienced reader's accuracy improved with no significant change in interpretation time (p = 0.786).
evidence.quote: Among experienced readers, accuracy was maintained, with a significant reduction in reading time (p < 0.001) when assisted by the algorithm.
evidence.sample_unit: subjects (758 training/internal validation from NIFD and ADNI; 89 external validation)

evidence.title: A Multiagent Large Language Model Framework for Emergency Treatment Recommendation in Acute Ischemic Stroke: Development and Validation Study
evidence.outcome: Physician treatment decision accuracy with versus without LLM support
evidence.effect: LLM support increased treatment decision accuracy from 73.1% to 88.6% (odds ratio 2.86, 95% CI, 2.27-3.60; P<.001); TOAST classification odds ratio 3.63.
evidence.quote: In the prospective physician study, LLM support increased treatment decision accuracy from 73.1% to 88.6% (odds ratio 2.86, 95% CI, 2.27-3.60; P<.001).
evidence.sample_unit: cases (1055 group A, 721 group B, 144 group C, 161 group D)

evidence.title: Missed Incidental Lung Cancer on Neck CT: Determinants and Impact on Diagnostic Delay and Stage Shift
evidence.outcome: AI-CAD detection of lung lesions missed by radiologists on neck CT
evidence.effect: AI-CAD detected 41 of 80 missed lesions (51.3%), without significant variations across imaging or lesion characteristics; standalone retrospective application, not with users.
evidence.quote: AI-CAD detected 41 of 80 missed lesions (51.3%), without significant variations across imaging or lesion characteristics.
evidence.sample_unit: patients with lung cancer visible on neck CT

evidence.title: Multimodal Large Language Models for Breast Ultrasound Report Auditing: Workflow-Error Detection, False-Positive Burden, and Limits of Key-Image Interpretation
evidence.venue: Journal of imaging informatics in medicine
evidence.outcome: LLM vs physician reader performance in report auditing; no human-with-AI arm
evidence.effect: Physician reader achieved 91.7% report-level sensitivity and 83.0% error-level recall without false positives; Gemini multimodal sensitivity 96.2% but false positives in 18/60 error-free reports.
evidence.quote: The physician reader achieved 91.7% report-level sensitivity and 83.0% error-level recall without false positives.
evidence.sample_unit: breast ultrasound examinations (300-report error-enriched subset for report auditing)

evidence.title: Divergent impacts of explainable AI for dermatological diagnosis on clinicians versus lay people
evidence.outcome: Performance of users with vs without AI and overreliance assessment
evidence.effect: AI assistance improved lay accuracy 69.7% to 75.8% and PCP top-1 accuracy +21.5%; overreliance appeared in lay users when AI erred (−23.3 points, β=-0.233).
evidence.quote: However, the general publicʼs diagnostic accuracy improved when AI provided correct predictions, whereas incorrect predictions reduced the performance significantly ( β = −0.233, 95% CI: −0.307 to −0.158, P < 0.001; Fig. 2d and Supplementary Table 12 ).

evidence.title: Determinants of Reader-LLM Interaction in Thoracic Radiology: Impact of Model Confidence and Reader Expertise
evidence.outcome: Reader adequate interaction and overreliance with versus without LLM assistance, by LLM accuracy and confidence
evidence.effect: Model confidence (OR 3.82) and reader expertise (OR 2.06) independently associated with adequate interaction; higher rationale quality increased acceptance of incorrect suggestions (OR 1.71) while reducing rejection of correct ones (OR 0.79).
evidence.quote: Higher rationale quality reduced rejection of correct suggestions (OR, 0.79 [95% CI: 0.67, 0.93]; P = .005) but increased acceptance of incorrect suggestions (OR, 1.71 [95% CI: 1.47, 1.99]; P < .001).
evidence.sample_unit: chest imaging cases (each read by 10 readers, 1000 reader-case pairs per session)

evidence.title: AI-Assisted Detection of Macular OCT Abnormalities by Optometrists: A Retrospective Reader Study
evidence.outcome: Optometrist sensitivity for OCT abnormalities with vs without AI assistance versus expert reference
evidence.effect: Sensitivity rose from 61.6% to 98.6% (Optometrist A, p<2.0x10-8) and from 87.7% to 95.9% (Optometrist B, p=0.031); accuracy 79.0% to 86.5% and 91.5% to 92.5%, with modest specificity reductions.
evidence.quote: Sensitivity improved from 61.6% (95% CI 49.5-72.8) to 98.6% (95% CI 92.6-100.0) for Optometrist A (p<2.0x10-8) and from 87.7% (95% CI 77.9-94.2) to 95.9% (95% CI 88.5-99.1) for Optometrist B (p=0.031).
evidence.sample_unit: macular OCT B-scans (one per patient), read by 2 optometrists

evidence.title: A Multidisciplinary Team-Based Large Language Model Framework for Predicting Postoperative Neurological Complications in Acute Type A Aortic Dissection: Model Development and Validation Study
evidence.outcome: Whether adding multidisciplinary-team multiagent layer improves LLM AUC over single-agent settings
evidence.effect: MDT with in-context learning GPT-5 had AUC 0.8419 vs unaided baseline (P=.006), but adding MDT within matched settings did not significantly improve AUC over single-agent settings in either cohort.
evidence.quote: Although this configuration showed a significantly higher AUC than the fully unaided GPT-5 baseline (P=.006), this improvement reflected the combined effect of MDT and in-context learning, as adding the MDT framework within matched settings did not significantly improve AUC over corresponding single-agent settings in either cohort.

evidence.title: A stacking model for AI-assisted diagnosis of suspected pituitary microadenomas on non-contrast T1COR MRI: a multicenter reader study on bridging the experience gap
evidence.outcome: Radiologist diagnostic accuracy unaided versus with AI assistance across experience levels
evidence.effect: AI assistance significantly improved accuracy across all experience levels; with combined model, seniors reached 75.4-79.0% in internal validation and up to 85.4% in hardest external cohort, ~30% absolute gain over unaided.
evidence.quote: In the reader study with 315 lesions and five radiologists, AI assistance significantly improved diagnostic accuracy across all experience levels.

evidence.title: Error Detection and Correction in Chinese Radiology Reports Using Large Language Models: Real-World Clinical Validation Study
evidence.outcome: LLM error detection performance compared with human readers of varying expertise
evidence.effect: DeepSeek-R1 detection 83% vs junior radiologists 80% (P=.39) and senior radiologists 78% (P=.19); better than nonradiologists 66% and nonphysicians 38% (P<.001). Standalone LLM only; no human-with-AI arm.
evidence.quote: DeepSeek-R1 showed performance comparable to radiologists (83%, 95% CI 76%-89% vs 80%, 95% CI 72%-86% for junior radiologists and 78%, 95% CI 70%-85% for senior radiologists; P=.39 and P=.19, respectively) and significantly better performance than that of nonradiologists and nonphysicians (83%, 95% CI 76%-89% vs 66%, 95% CI 57%-74% and 38%, 95% CI 30%-47%; P<.001, respectively).

evidence.title: Physician-revised AI-generated drafts are associated with higher ratings of written explanations in end-of-life care in the intensive care unit: a scenario-based single-center cross-sectional study
evidence.outcome: Compared physician-with-AI collaboration against physician alone and AI alone on rated quality

evidence.quote: Thus, the higher ratings of physician–AI collaborative responses were consistent across analyses, whereas the difference between physician-only and AI-only responses depended on the analytic approach.

evidence.title: Comparing individual and peer-supported ChatGPT use in nursing case analysis: Effects on nursing diagnostic skills and cognitive load in a randomized controlled trial
evidence.outcome: nursing diagnostic skills
evidence.effect: Diagnostic skills improved after the intervention, but there was no significant interaction effect among the groups (p = .936).
evidence.quote: Although students' nursing diagnostic skills improved after the intervention, we did not observe a significant interaction effect among the groups (p = .936).

evidence.title: Evaluation of a cornea-specialized large language model for diagnostic and management accuracy in complex corneal cases
evidence.outcome: Clinician management accuracy with versus without AI assistance
evidence.effect: Management accuracy inconsistent: Ophthalmologist 3 improved to 71.8% (p<0.05), Ophthalmologist 1 remained 82.1%, Ophthalmologist 2 declined to 64.1% (p<0.05) from 87.2%.
evidence.quote: With the specialized model, Ophthalmologist 3 improved to 71.8% (p<0.05), Ophthalmologist 1 remained high at 82.1%, and Ophthalmologist 2 declined to 64.1% (p<0.05).
evidence.sample_unit: cornea trainees (each reviewing 39 real-world corneal cases under three conditions)

evidence.title: Clinical usability of an explainable AI decision support tool and evaluation of multimodal models in NSCLC
evidence.outcome: Physician prediction accuracy with versus without XAI decision support tool
evidence.effect: Lung expert and nonexpert physicians improved their prediction when using the XAI ML CB-only tool; no numbers given in the abstract.
evidence.quote: The clinical usability study showed that lung expert and nonexpert physicians improved their prediction with the explainable AI (XAI) ML CB-only based tool.

evidence.title: Locally Deployed Large Language Models for AI-Assisted Outpatient Prescription Review: Crossover Study
evidence.outcome: Pharmacist review accuracy and sensitivity with vs without AI assistance
evidence.effect: Accuracy 97.2% (207/213) collaborative vs 82.6% (176/213) alone (P<.001); sensitivity 98% vs 55%; false-negative rate 45% to 2%
evidence.quote: Overall review accuracy was 97.2% (207/213, 95% CI 94.0%-98.7%) in the human-AI collaborative condition vs 82.6% (176/213, 95% CI 77.0%-87.1%) in the pharmacist-alone condition (P<.001).

evidence.title: Evaluating Artificial Intelligence as a First-Pass Reader in Fundus Photograph Screening: A Multireader Workflow Validation Study
evidence.outcome: Sensitivity/specificity of AI-human double reading versus human-human double reading, plus human reads per image
evidence.effect: DR/RVO: no significant difference (all p≥0.05). AMD: sensitivity 0.916 and 0.950 (p<0.001) vs 0.845, one combination 0.842 (p=0.742); human reads 1.02-1.11 vs 2.00-2.10 per image.
evidence.quote: Across AI-human combinations, sensitivity and specificity did not differ significantly from human-human reading (all p ≥ 0.05; specificity differences ≤0.001).

evidence.title: [Attention-based multi-task deep learning model for predicting the primary site of cervical metastatic squamous cell carcinoma with unknown primary]
evidence.venue: Zhonghua er bi yan hou tou jing wai ke za zhi = Chinese journal of otorhinolaryngology head and neck surgery
evidence.outcome: Junior physician primary-site prediction accuracy with versus without model assistance in real-world CMSCCUP cohort
evidence.effect: Model achieved Micro-AUC 0.809 and Top-3 accuracy 88% in the real-world cohort (172 cases), significantly improving junior physicians' predictive accuracy (all P<0.001).
evidence.quote: In a real-world CMSCCUP cohort (172 cases, including 86 CMSCCUP patients and 86 normal controls), the model achieved a Micro-AUC of 0.809 against the gold standard and a Top-3 accuracy of 88%, significantly improving the predictive accuracy of junior physicians (all P<0.001).
evidence.sample_unit: patients with known-primary cervical lymph node metastases (training and test sets)

commentary.bottom_line: Among the supplied studies, twelve randomized trials and eighteen prospective or quasi-experimental studies compared clinicians with and without AI in live deployment, with results ranging from clear gains to no difference, and several found that human-AI team performance departed from standalone AI performance in both directions. No study tested whether running such evaluations changes purchasing or deployment decisions, and few measured overreliance directly.

perspectives.view: Twelve randomized trials in real deployment compared users with and without AI. Most favored AI assistance, but two found no significant difference in sensitivity or miss rate, and one cluster trial reported a 55.1% misdiagnosis rate despite AI alerts. These trials test specific tools rather than the evaluation practice, so certainty is downgraded for indirectness and inconsistency.

Standalone AI produced 381 false positives in 634 patients, yet radiologists reported one, so team performance exceeded the model alone. In other settings the reverse held. Assisted schedulers underperformed the model alone, and radiologists with discretionary AI reached 90.0% fracture sensitivity against 93.5% for standalone AI. Standalone figures may mislead in either direction.

Error profiles changed with deployment mode, as triage, safety-net, and problem-solving workflows produced different false-negative and false-positive rates from standalone AI. Automation bias degraded multi-reader but improved single-reader screening in one replay study. Clinicians followed 86% of predictions when half were wrong. Most live trials, including one ophthalmology trial, did not report overreliance.

A simulation modeled on low-income women found that as reliance on AI rose, false-negative rates moved from 27.11% versus 26.74% to 18.79% versus 33.33% for privileged and unprivileged groups. This suggests that team evaluations may need subgroup reporting. Only two live tests included limited English proficiency populations.

FDA draft guidance states that both standalone and human-device team evaluations may support a performance claim, and the radiology multi-society statement calls for evaluating the radiologist-plus-AI combination. The supplied studies show that such team evaluations can be conducted in live practice, though none tests how regulators or purchasers used the results.

The largest deployment-mode trials enrolled 105,915 and 10,476 screened patients, which suggests that adequately powered team evaluations may require substantial volume and time. One crossover trial reported 16.7 versus 14.1 daily exams on AI days. No study reported the cost or staffing needed to run the evaluation itself.

commentary.research_gap: No study compared deployment decisions or patient outcomes between organizations that conducted human-with-versus-without-AI evaluations and those that relied on standalone metrics. Few live trials measured overreliance, such as acceptance of incorrect AI outputs, and none reported the cost of conducting team evaluations.
commentary.underserved_note: Two live tests included limited English proficiency populations, a Chinese primary care diabetic retinopathy study and a United States medication identification study of 41 patients. One screening study included rural patients. No test included Medicaid or safety-net populations or reported low-literacy participants, and the only low-income evidence comes from a simulation that documented the hazard. Health systems serving these groups therefore cannot assume that team performance reported elsewhere will transfer.
